milestone: By 2013 (age 21), her coming out as transgender video went viral with 4.1M views; by 2017 (age 25), she was the subject of a Barbara Kopple documentary premiering at Sundance; by 2018 (age 26), she had ~2.5M subscribers.

name: Eva Gutowski
milestone: By 2014 (age 20), she had 240K+ subscribers and a deal with Seventeen magazine; by 2017 (age 23), she had 7.5M subscribers, a YouTube Red series, and a forthcoming book; by 2020 (age 26), she had 11M+ subscribers.

name: Safiya Nygaard
milestone: By 2015 (age 23), she was hired as a video producer at BuzzFeed and co-created the LadyLike series; by 2017 (age 25), her solo YouTube channel reached 2.5M+ subscribers in 6 months after leaving BuzzFeed; by 2018 (age 26), she had millions more.

name: Simone Giertz
milestone: By November 2015 (age 25), her 'Breakfast Machine' and 'Wake-up Machine' videos each received 1M+ views; by 2016 (age 25-26), she had ~200K subscribers, 10M+ total views, appeared on The Late Show with Stephen Colbert, and began working with Adam Savage.

name: Lindsey Stirling
milestone: Her music video 'Crystallize' became the 8th most-watched YouTube video of 2012 with over 42M views, and her self-released debut album 'Lindsey Stirling' launched in September 2012, selling 108K+ copies by mid-2013; she had 700K+ YouTube subscribers by August 2012 and a sold-out European tour.

name: Todrick Hall
milestone: By 2008, his YouTube channel reached 2 million subscribers with viral videos; he was cast in Broadway's The Color Purple at age 20 and later in Memphis; he reached the Top 16 of American Idol Season 9 in 2010, all before turning 26 in April 2011.

name: Ryan Higa
milestone: Co-created the nigahiga YouTube channel in 2006 at age 16; it became the most-subscribed channel on YouTube from 2009 to 2011 and was the first channel to reach 3 million subscribers in December 2010; by age 26 in 2016, the channel had 20+ million subscribers.

name: Kevin Wu
milestone: By May 2008 at age 17, he became the number one subscribed comedian on YouTube and third most subscribed overall with 187K subscribers; by 2014, his channel had 3M+ subscribers and 350M+ views, all well before age 26 in June 2016.

name: Ian Hecox
milestone: Co-founded Smosh in 2005 at age 18; their Pokémon Theme video became the most-viewed YouTube video; Smosh became the most-subscribed YouTube channel on three separate occasions; by 2011, Smosh was acquired by Defy Media, and by age 26 in 2013, the channel had millions of subscribers.

name: Anthony Padilla
milestone: Co-founded Smosh in 2005 at age 18; registered smosh.com in 2002; their Pokémon Theme video became the most-viewed YouTube video; Smosh became the most-subscribed YouTube channel on three occasions; by 2011, Smosh was acquired by Defy Media, and by age 26 in 2013, the channel had millions of subscribers.

name: Freddie Wong
milestone: Launched YouTube channel in 2006; won first prize in Guitar Hero 2 at the World Series of Video Games in 2007; appeared on MTV's TRL in 2007; formed RocketJump production company in 2011 and raised $273K on Kickstarter for Video Game High School; the freddiew channel had millions of subscribers by age 26 in September 2011.

name: Philip DeFranco
milestone: Created his YouTube account in September 2006 at age 20; by 2008, his sxephil channel was the 5th most-subscribed on YouTube; by October 2012, he had 2M subscribers and ~30M monthly views; by age 26 in December 2011, he was one of YouTube's most established creators.

name: MatPat
milestone: Launched Game Theory on April 18, 2011 at age 24; the channel rapidly gained subscribers and was featured on the front pages of ScrewAttack and GameTrailers; by age 26 in November 2012, the channel had a substantial and growing audience, and it reached 1 million subscribers in December 2013 at age 27.

name: Toby Turner
milestone: Joined YouTube in May 2006 at age 21; created viral videos including 'Don't Tase Me, Bro!' remix; started daily vlogs in April 2009; launched TobyGames channel in July 2010; by age 26 in March 2011, he had three active YouTube channels with a combined following in the millions.

name: Bart Baker
milestone: Started YouTube channel in 2009 after college; reached 100K subscribers in 2011; by VidCon 2012 at age 26, had approximately 170K subscribers; was signed with Maker Studios and monetizing parody videos; reached 1M subscribers in 2013.

name: Scott Wozniak
milestone: Scott the Woz YouTube channel hit 100,000 subscribers by 2018 (age 21) and grew to 2M+ subscribers by 2023 (age 26), with the series syndicated on the G4 television network in 2021.

name: Arin Hanson
milestone: Hanson's 'Metal Gear Awesome' animation on Newgrounds (Feb 2006, age 19) led to MTV commissioning animated shorts, and he co-founded Game Grumps in July 2012 (age 25), which became one of YouTube's most popular Let's Play channels.

name: JonTron
milestone: Jafari created the JonTronShow YouTube channel in August 2010 (age 20), co-founded NormalBoots in late 2010, and co-created Game Grumps in July 2012 (age 22), building a channel that reached millions of subscribers well before age 26.

name: ProJared
milestone: Knabenbauer joined ScrewAttack in 2009 (age 24) where he hosted and produced multiple gaming shows including Nametags, Hard News, and Reboot or Retro, and launched his ProJared YouTube channel in 2010 (age 25), establishing his online presence before age 26.

name: Grace Helbig
milestone: Helbig launched DailyGrace on My Damn Channel in April 2008 (age 22), which grew to over 2.4 million YouTube subscribers by December 2013; she became a G4 correspondent in 2011 (age 25-26), establishing herself as a leading YouTube comedian before age 26.

name: Hannah Hart
milestone: Hart launched My Drunk Kitchen on YouTube in March 2011 (age 24), which gathered 800K views by July 2011 and grew to 2.3M+ subscribers by June 2015; she won a Streamy Award for Best Female Performance in a Comedy in 2013 (age 26).

name: Timothy DeLaGhetto
milestone: Chantarangsu launched his YouTube channel in 2006 (age 20), hit 1 million subscribers by August 2011 (age 25), and had 2.7M+ subscribers by 2015; he was cast on MTV's Wild 'N Out in 2013 (age 27), just after the age-26 window, but his YouTube milestone was well established before 26.

name: Ricky Dillon
milestone: Dillon started his YouTube channel in 2009 (age 17), joined the O2L supergroup which amassed 2.7M subscribers before disbanding in December 2014, and by age 26 (2018) had 2.9M+ subscribers on his solo channel with a debut album 'Gold' released in January 2016.

name: Ryland Adams
milestone: Adams created his YouTube channel in February 2010 (age 18) and became an on-air host and producer for Clevver Media in 2014 (age 23), helping the pop culture news channel amass over 3.4M subscribers; by age 26 (May 2017), he had established his personal brand and begun his own vlog channel.

name: Andrew Siwicki
milestone: Siwicki became the full-time cinematographer and editor for Shane Dawson's massively viewed documentary series in 2017-2018 (age 25-26), including 'The Truth About Tanacon,' 'The Secret World of Jeffree Star,' and 'The Mind of Jake Paul,' which collectively garnered hundreds of millions of views; he also amassed 1M+ Instagram followers by 2018.

name: Rachel Ballinger
milestone: Ballinger started her YouTube channel in September 2006 (age 15) and uploaded her first video in June 2007, building a following through her 'You Know What Pisses Me Off' series; by age 26 (April 2017), she had 2M+ subscribers and published her first book '101 Things That Piss Me Off' in June 2017.

name: Ilan Ramon
milestone: Graduated from the Israel Air Force Flight Academy as a fighter pilot at age 20 in 1974, having already served in the Yom Kippur War in 1973.

name: Luka Dončić
milestone: Won the 2018 EuroLeague championship and EuroLeague MVP at age 19 with Real Madrid, becoming the youngest MVP in EuroLeague history.

name: Adam Małysz
milestone: Won his first Ski Jumping World Cup event in Oslo on March 17, 1996 at age 18, followed by multiple World Cup victories in Sapporo and Hakuba in January 1997 at age 19.

name: Nick Ut
milestone: Won the 1973 Pulitzer Prize for Spot News Photography at age 22 for 'The Terror of War' (Napalm Girl), one of the most iconic photographs of the 20th century, taken on June 8, 1972 when he was 21.

name: Marlene Dumas
milestone: Had her work included in a group show at the Stedelijk Museum Amsterdam in 1978 at age 25, with her first museum sale ('Don't Talk to Strangers') purchased by the Stedelijk, one of Europe's premier modern art museums.

name: Mikkel Hansen
milestone: Won the Danish handball championship with GOG in 2007 at age 19, made his Danish national team debut the same year, and joined FC Barcelona in 2008 at 20. By 24, he was named IHF World Player of the Year (2011).

name: Michael Stevens
milestone: Vsauce channel reached 100K subscribers by January 2011 (age 24-25), 500K by January 2012 (age 25-26), and 1 million subscribers by September 2012 (age 26), making it one of the fastest-growing educational channels on YouTube.

name: Amanda Steele
milestone: Steele started her YouTube channel MakeupByMandy24 in 2010 at age 10-11, reached approximately 25K subscribers by age 13 with her first brand deal (K-Mart) and mall meet-up, and grew to nearly 3 million subscribers by age 16 with IMG Models signing, a Quay Australia sunglass line, and starring role in Hulu's Guidance web series.

name: Claudia Sulewski
milestone: Sulewski reached 1 million subscribers on her YouTube channel BeyondBeautyStar in early 2015 at age 18-19, and was named Teen Vogue's first-ever YouTube host in February 2015, a landmark Conde Nast partnership for a digital creator.

name: Sara Dietschy
milestone: Dietschy's YouTube channel skyrocketed from 4K to 100K subscribers in 2016 after her 'How to Casey Neistat a Vlog' video went viral and received a shout-out from Casey Neistat. She became an Adobe Creative Resident in 2016, and by 2018 had over 550K subscribers with major brand partnerships.

name: Brandon Calvillo
milestone: Calvillo amassed over 100K followers on Vine by late spring 2013 at age 19, and grew to over 2 million Vine followers with sponsored content deals from MTV and other brands earning $1K-$10K per video, establishing himself as one of the platform's top creators well before age 26.

name: Brent Rivera
milestone: Rivera joined Vine in 2013 at age 15 and gained 2 million followers within a year, growing to 8.5 million Vine followers by 2016. He hit 1 million YouTube subscribers in March 2015 at age 17, and co-founded Amp Studios which generated 10 billion monthly social media views by 2020.

name: Larray
milestone: Larray reached 100K YouTube subscribers in 2017 at age 19, 1 million subscribers in 2018 at age 20, and was nominated for Breakout Creator at the 9th Streamy Awards in December 2019. His novelty songs spent 42 weeks on Billboard's Comedy Digital Tracks chart, with 'First Place' gaining over 41 million YouTube views.

name: Destin Conrad
milestone: Conrad amassed over 1 million followers on Vine by approximately 2015-2016 at age 15-16, making him a member of the 'million follower club' on the platform. He later transitioned to a music career, releasing his debut EP Colorway in 2021 and receiving a Grammy nomination for Best Progressive R&B Album in 2025.

name: Inanna Sarkis
milestone: Sarkis had 1.7 million YouTube subscribers by 2017 at age 24, with a Sprint campaign deal, WWE collaboration, and feature film debut in Tyler Perry's Boo 2! A Madea Halloween. By 2019 at age 26, she had 3.7M subscribers and starred in the film After, a major theatrical release.

name: Meg Turney
milestone: Turney joined SourceFed as a host in 2012 at age 25, a major YouTube news channel with over 1.3 million subscribers. She also appeared on Syfy's Heroes of Cosplay and hosted a cosplay contest at SXSW 2013, establishing herself as a notable internet personality by age 26.

name: Jazz Jennings
milestone: Jennings received national attention at age 7 in 2007 through a Barbara Walters interview on 20/20, co-founded the TransKids Purple Rainbow Foundation, starred in the TLC reality series I Am Jazz premiering in 2015 at age 14, was named to Time's 25 Most Influential Teens, received LogoTV's Youth Trailblazer Award, and published a memoir at age 16.

name: Cameron Dallas
milestone: Had 8.1 million Vine followers by 2014, starred in the AwesomenessTV film Expelled, and headlined the Magcon touring convention — all before age 21.

name: Nash Grier
milestone: Became the second most-followed user on Vine with 12.4 million followers by 2015, at age 17, making him one of the platform's biggest stars.

name: Hayes Grier
milestone: Had 4 million Vine followers and competed on Dancing with the Stars at age 15, signing with CAA and inking deals with Aeropostale and Verizon.

name: King Bach
milestone: Became the most-followed user on Vine with 16.2 million followers by March 2015 at age 26, having already gained millions of followers and recurring TV roles by age 25.

name: Lele Pons
milestone: Became the first Vine star to hit 1 billion loops in 2014 at age 18, and was the most followed woman on Vine with 11.5 million followers.

name: Amanda Cerny
milestone: Was named Playboy Playmate of the Month in October 2011 at age 20, and subsequently built over 4.6 million Vine followers by her mid-twenties.

name: Hannah Stocking
milestone: Had a viral Vine video that gained 100K followers overnight, and by 2015-2016 appeared in major music videos (G-Eazy, Blink-182) and had a significant Vine following, all before age 25.

name: Juanpa Zurita
milestone: Had 1.8 million Vine followers by 2017 and modeled for Calvin Klein, Louis Vuitton, and Dolce & Gabbana in 2016 at age 20, making him one of Latin America's biggest digital creators.

name: Rudy Mancuso
milestone: Had over 10 million Vine followers by the time Vine shut down in 2016 at age 24, and appeared on Comedy Central's Drunk History in 2015, establishing himself as one of Vine's leading stars.

name: Anwar Jibawi
milestone: Was ranked among the top 100 most-followed Viners by 2015 at age 24, with his first video blowing up overnight and building a following that reached 6 million+ on YouTube after Vine's shutdown.

name: Thomas Sanders
milestone: Reached 1 million Vine followers by September 2013 at age 24 and 5.8 million by May 2015, winning the 2015 Shorty Award for Viner of the Year, with 8.3 million followers and 7.4 billion loops by Vine's shutdown.

name: Shawn Mendes
milestone: Signed with Island Records at 15 in May 2014, debuted at #24 on Billboard with 'Life of the Party,' and released debut album Handwritten in 2015 at age 16 which debuted at #1 on the Billboard 200 — making him one of five artists ever to debut at #1 before age 18.

name: Vladimir Drinfeld
milestone: Won a gold medal with full marks at the 1969 International Mathematical Olympiad at age 15; by age 24 had defended his PhD at Moscow University and proved the Langlands conjecture for GL(2) over function fields, a landmark result in number theory.

name: Margaret Gardiner
milestone: Won Miss Universe 1978 at age 18, becoming the first South African and first African woman to win the title.

name: Laura Cutina
milestone: Won a team silver medal at the 1983 World Championships at age 15 and an Olympic team gold medal at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics at age 16.

name: Chantal Akerman
milestone: Made her first short film 'Saute ma ville' at age 18 in 1968, which premiered at the International Short Film Festival Oberhausen in 1971.

name: Robert Zemeckis
milestone: Won a Student Academy Award (Special Jury Prize) for his short film 'A Field of Honor' at USC in 1973, which caught the attention of Steven Spielberg.

name: Piero Gros
milestone: Won his first two World Cup races in December 1972 at age 18, becoming the youngest Italian skier ever to win a World Cup race; won the overall World Cup title in 1974 at age 19.

name: Wanderlei Silva
milestone: Won the inaugural PRIDE Middleweight Championship on November 3, 2001 at age 25, defeating Kazushi Sakuraba at PRIDE 17.

name: Kurt Cobain
milestone: Released Nirvana's second album 'Nevermind' on DGC Records in September 1991 at age 24, which topped the Billboard charts and became a global cultural phenomenon.

name: Jaiden Animations
milestone: Reached 1 million YouTube subscribers in December 2016 at age 19, growing to 10 million by June 2021 at age 23, and won a Streamy Award for Animated category in 2020.

name: TheOdd1sOut
milestone: Reached approximately 600,000 YouTube subscribers by 2016 at age 20, growing to millions by his mid-20s, and co-created and executive produced the Netflix animated series Oddballs in 2022 at age 26.

name: Alan Becker
milestone: Created 'Animator vs. Animation' which went viral on Newgrounds in June 2006 at age 17, received funding from AtomFilms for a sequel, and established a massively popular YouTube channel with billions of views by his mid-20s.

name: Domics
milestone: Joined Channel Frederator Network in November 2014 at age 24, had a growing YouTube channel with millions of views by 2016 at age 25-26, and reached 5+ million subscribers in subsequent years.

name: Dream
milestone: Reached 1 million YouTube subscribers in 2020 at age 20, growing to 30+ million by 2021 at age 22, won Streamy Awards for Gaming in 2020 and 2021, and the Game Awards Content Creator of the Year in 2021.

name: GeorgeNotFound
milestone: Co-founded the Dream SMP in 2020 at age 23, reached 10+ million YouTube subscribers by 2022 at age 25, and earned a Guinness World Record for most viewers of a cooking livestream on Twitch.

name: Sapnap
milestone: Uploaded first YouTube video in October 2019 at age 18, became a founding member of the Dream SMP in early 2020, reached millions of subscribers and Twitch followers by 2021 at age 19-20, and co-owned NRG Esports from 2022 at age 21.

name: TommyInnit
milestone: Joined the Dream SMP on July 4, 2020 at age 16, surpassed 1 billion YouTube views at age 17, broke two Guinness World Records for most followed Minecraft channel on Twitch and most-watched Minecraft stream, and reached 15+ million YouTube subscribers and 9+ million Twitch followers by age 19.

name: Tubbo
milestone: Reached 1 million Twitch followers by November 21, 2020 at age 16, became a key character on the Dream SMP in 2020, and grew to 5+ million Twitch followers by his late teens, making him one of the most-followed Minecraft streamers on the platform.

name: Wilbur Soot
milestone: Co-founded SootHouse which reached 1 million subscribers in May 2019 at age 22, launched his solo channel which reached 1 million subscribers by April 2020 at age 23, and became a lead writer on the Dream SMP in 2020, founding the fictional nation of L'Manberg.

name: Technoblade
milestone: Rose to popularity in 2019 at age 20 by winning multiple Minecraft Monday tournaments, joined the Dream SMP in 2020, won a $100,000 MrBeast duel against Dream, and reached 10 million YouTube subscribers by late 2021 at age 22 before his death in June 2022.

name: Ranboo
milestone: Reached 1 million YouTube subscribers by January 2021 at age 17, joined the Dream SMP on November 27, 2020 at age 17, and grew to 4+ million Twitch followers, becoming one of the most popular Minecraft streamers on the platform.

name: Nihachu
milestone: Appeared on AustinShow's Love or Host in early 2020 at age 18, going from 300 to 15,000 Twitch followers overnight, and joined the Dream SMP in August 2020, reaching 2.6 million Twitch followers by 2022 at age 20.

name: Quackity
milestone: Joined the Dream SMP in August 2020 at age 19 after TommyInnit's recommendation, experiencing tremendous rapid growth to 6 million Twitch followers, and won Best Minecraft Streamer at the 2022 Streamer Awards at age 21.

name: Karl Jacobs
milestone: Became an on-screen cast member of MrBeast's channel in January 2020 at age 21 and joined the Dream SMP in August 2020, growing to 3.5 million Twitch followers and 6.95 million YouTube subscribers by 2023 at age 24.

name: Chris Tyson
milestone: Co-founded the MrBeast YouTube channel in 2012 at age 16 and appeared as core co-host from 2015, with the channel surpassing 100 million subscribers by 2022 when Tyson was 26, alongside millions of personal social media followers.

name: Corpse Husband
milestone: Hit 5 million YouTube subscribers in late 2020 at age 23 riding Among Us virality, with music single 'E-GIRLS ARE RUINING MY LIFE' gaining over 93 million Spotify streams, and reached 7 million subscribers by early 2021 at age 24.

name: Shroud
milestone: Signed by Cloud9 as a permanent CS:GO player in August 2014 at age 20, building a streaming audience of 40,000+ regular viewers, and won Content Creator of the Year at The Game Awards 2019 at age 25, reaching 11 million Twitch followers by age 26.

name: Tfue
milestone: Joined FaZe Clan in April 2018 at age 20, becoming one of the biggest Fortnite streamers with 11.5 million Twitch followers and earning over $20 million from gaming, endorsements, and sponsorships by the time he was 21.

name: Pokimane
milestone: Co-founded OfflineTV in 2017 at age 21, won Shorty Award for Twitch Streamer of the Year in 2018 at age 22, and reached 5.4 million Twitch followers by 2020 at age 24, growing to 9.5 million by 2026 as the most-followed female streamer on the platform.

name: xQc
milestone: Joined Dallas Fuel in the Overwatch League in October 2017 at age 21, and after transitioning to full-time streaming in 2018, reached 9 million Twitch followers by 2020 at age 25, becoming one of the most-watched streamers on the platform.

name: Asmongold
milestone: Broke 100,000 Twitch followers in 2016 at age 26, building on years of World of Warcraft YouTube guides starting in 2008-2009, and reaching 200,000 followers by end of 2016, establishing himself as a top WoW content creator.

name: Summit1g
milestone: Reached 51,000 Twitch followers by October 2013 at age 26 as a Twitch partner with 1,400 daily viewers, qualifying as a material milestone of 50K+ followers with revenue, while competing as a professional CS:GO player.

name: Mark Hunt
milestone: Won the K-1 Oceania Tournament in February 2000 at age 25, qualifying for the K-1 World Grand Prix with a 15-4 professional kickboxing record.

name: Jiang Jialiang
milestone: Won team gold, doubles silver, and singles bronze at the 1983 World Table Tennis Championships in Tokyo at age 19; went on to win World Cup singles in 1984 and World Championships singles gold in 1985 and 1987, all before age 26.

name: Peter Blangé
milestone: Won a bronze medal at the 1989 European Volleyball Championship with the Netherlands at age 24, as part of a national team career that began at age 19 in 1984.

name: Raimo Helminen
milestone: Won silver at the 1984 U20 World Championship, breaking the tournament scoring record and making the All-Star team at age 19; also competed at the 1984 Sarajevo Olympics that same year.

name: Myth
milestone: By June 2018 at age 19, had over 3.2 million Twitch followers and was captain of Team SoloMid's Fortnite roster after explosive growth from Fortnite streaming in late 2017.

name: Scarra
milestone: Became professional League of Legends mid-laner for Team Dignitas in September 2011 at age 21, one of the most recognized LoL pros of the early LCS era, later coaching CLG in 2014-2015.

name: Fanum
milestone: Co-founded AMP (Any Means Possible) in October 2019 at age 22, which surpassed 1 million YouTube subscribers by mid-2021; won Best Roleplay Streamer at the 2022 Streamer Awards and Breakout Streamer of the Year at the 2023 Streamy Awards at age 25-26.

name: Duke Dennis
milestone: Reached 100,000 YouTube subscribers by 2018 at age 24 and co-founded AMP in October 2019 at age 25, building a foundational content collective that surpassed 1 million subscribers by mid-2021.

name: PointCrow
milestone: Grew to over 2 million YouTube subscribers and approximately 600K Twitch followers by 2023 at age 25, building a major Nintendo challenge content brand with viral Breath of the Wild videos.

name: SmallAnt
milestone: Won Speedrunner of the Year at the 2021 Streamer Awards at age 25 and held multiple world records in Super Mario Odyssey Minimum Captures category, establishing himself as one of the biggest speedrunning content creators.

name: Alpharad
milestone: Became the first Smash Bros YouTuber to reach 1 million subscribers on November 22, 2018 at age 22, establishing himself as one of the most well-known Smash Bros content creators with over 3.6 million subscribers by 2025.

name: BoxBox
milestone: Built a Twitch following of over 1.8 million followers and became one of the most popular League of Legends streamers by the early 2020s, known for Riven gameplay and champion cosplay, after starting streaming in 2012 and joining Velocity eSports in 2013.

name: QuarterJade
milestone: Joined OfflineTV as an official member in November 2021 at age 24, bringing approximately 1 million Twitch followers into the premier streaming collective, after being invited to Streamer Camp 2018 and building a substantial audience through PUBG and Valorant content.

name: Masayoshi
milestone: Joined OfflineTV as an official member in November 2021 at age 24 after achieving Twitch partnership in March 2019 and building a following through League of Legends and Valorant streams and collaborations with other streamers.

name: Sydeon
milestone: Joined OfflineTV as an official member in November 2021 at age 24 with approximately 250,000 Twitch followers, after becoming StockX's first gaming partner in September 2021 and building an audience through Minecraft gameplay and cosplay content.

name: TimTheTatman
milestone: Became a full-time sponsored Twitch streamer by March 2014 at age 23, with thousands of concurrent viewers and deals with Monster Energy and Audio-Technica; by 2016 at age 26, was one of the platform's top variety streamers with well over 100K followers.

name: NICKMERCS
milestone: Won the Gears of War 2 national championship in 2009 at age 18 with over $100K in total tournament earnings, and by 2016 at age 26 was one of the biggest Call of Duty streamers on Twitch with hundreds of thousands of followers, having joined 100 Thieves that year.

name: Valkyrae
milestone: Had her breakthrough playing Fortnite in 2018 and became the first female content creator for 100 Thieves in October 2018 at age 26, establishing herself as one of the top female streamers on Twitch.

name: LilyPichu
milestone: Went viral on YouTube with parody song 'I'll Quit LoL' in 2011 at age 19, and by 2017 at age 25-26 was a member of OfflineTV with millions of YouTube subscribers and Twitch followers, having released her debut EP 'Lilies' in 2015.

name: Disguised Toast
milestone: Joined OfflineTV in October 2017 at age 25 and was on Blizzard's A-list for Hearthstone by mid-2017, with hundreds of thousands of Twitch followers gained through viral Reddit-shared infographics and YouTube content; reached the stratosphere of Twitch streaming by late 2017.

name: Hasan Piker
milestone: Created and hosted 'The Breakdown' political video series on TYT Network in 2016 at age 24-25, and was a host and producer at The Young Turks while contributing to HuffPost from 2016 to 2018, all before age 26.

name: Ludwig Ahgren
milestone: Broke the all-time Twitch subscriber record with approximately 282,000 subscribers during his 30-day subathon event from March 14 to April 13, 2021 at age 25, surpassing Ninja's previous record; both his YouTube and Twitch channels had reached over 1 million followers by December 2020.

name: MoistCr1TiKaL
milestone: Had 2 million YouTube subscribers by March 2018 at age 23, co-hosted The Official Podcast from December 2016, and by 2020 at age 26 had grown to become one of the most established gaming commentators on YouTube with media coverage from The Guardian, Kotaku, and Daily Dot, plus a viral video featured by the Press Association.

name: Kai Cenat
milestone: Won Streamer of the Year at the 12th Streamy Awards in December 2022 at age 20, released a Gold-certified single with NLE Choppa, and by 2023 at age 21 became the most-subscribed Twitch streamer of all time with 306,621 subscribers during his Mafiathon subathon; currently age 24 with 20.5 million Twitch followers and estimated $8.5M annual earnings.

name: IShowSpeed
milestone: Grew from 100K to 1 million YouTube subscribers between April and June 2021 at age 16, won Breakout Streamer of the Year at the 12th Streamy Awards in 2022 at age 17, signed with Warner Records and charted with 'World Cup' single; currently age 21 with 59.2 million YouTube subscribers and 9.8 billion views.

name: Adin Ross
milestone: Trending #make2kfunagain worldwide on Twitter in November 2020 at age 20, gaining over 1 million Twitch followers by early 2021 with approximately 30,000 live viewers per stream, and having #FreeAdin trend on Twitter in April 2021; currently age 25 with 7 million Twitch followers and 4.61 million YouTube subscribers.

name: Ceb (Sébastien Debs)
milestone: Won The International 2018 as a player with OG at age 26, having previously coached OG to four Dota Major championships (Frankfurt, Manila, Boston, Kiev); also won The International 2019 for a second TI title.

name: KuroKy (Kuro Salehi Takhasomi)
milestone: Won The International 2017 with Team Liquid as captain at age 24; began professional DotA career at 16, competed at the inaugural TI in 2011, and reached TI Grand Finals three times by age 26.

name: Puppey (Clement Ivanov)
milestone: Won The International 2011 with Natus Vincere at age 21 for a $1M prize; founded Team Secret in 2014 at age 24; reached multiple TI finals and won a Dota Major by age 26, establishing himself as one of the most decorated Dota 2 captains.

name: Dendi (Danil Ishutin)
milestone: Won The International 2011 with Natus Vincere at age 21 for $1M; placed 2nd at TI 2012 and TI 2013; won multiple StarLadder championships and was featured in the 2014 documentary 'Free to Play' — all before age 26.

name: Miracle- (Amer Al-Barkawi)
milestone: Won the Frankfurt Major 2015 at age 18 and Manila Major 2016 with OG; became the first player to reach 9000 MMR in Dota 2 history (May 2016); won The International 2017 with Team Liquid at age 20 — all well before age 26.

name: SumaiL (Syed Sumail Hassan)
milestone: Won The International 2015 with Evil Geniuses at age 16, becoming the youngest player ever to win TI and the youngest esports player to earn over $1M in prize money; also won DAC 2015 — all well before age 26.

name: Arteezy (Artour Babaev)
milestone: Made professional debut at MLG Columbus 2013 at age 17, joined Evil Geniuses in 2014, placed 3rd at TI 2014 winning ~$1M; built one of the largest Twitch followings in Dota 2 (835K followers) by age 26; multiple top TI placements with EG.

name: Jaedong (Lee Jae-dong)
milestone: Won five OSL/MSL premier titles (3x OSL, 2x MSL) and WCG 2009 championship by age 26; debuted as a professional Brood War player in 2006 at age 16, winning Rookie of the Year; inducted into Korean esports Hall of Fame in 2012.

name: Flash (Lee Young-ho)
milestone: Won the Bacchus OSL 2008 at age 15, becoming the youngest Starleague champion in history; won 3 OSL and 3 MSL titles by age 19; widely regarded as the greatest Brood War player of all time and the fifth Bonjwa; inducted into Korean esports Hall of Fame in 2012.

name: SonicFox (Dominique McLean)
milestone: Won EVO 2014 (Injustice) at age 16, first of eight EVO championships across five game franchises; named Esports Player of the Year at The Game Awards 2018; included in Forbes 30 Under 30 (2020); highest-paid fighting game player in the world by age 22 — all before age 26.

name: Hungrybox (Juan Manuel DeBiedma)
milestone: Won Apex 2010 at age 16 and Revival of Melee 2 at age 16; became one of the 'Five Gods of Melee'; won EVO 2016; ranked #1 player in the world in 2010, 2017, 2018, and 2019; co-owner of Team Liquid since December 2021 — all milestones before or around age 26.

name: Nam Hyun-hee
milestone: Won gold medal in individual foil at the 2001 Asian Fencing Championships in Bangkok, and followed with team gold at the 2002 Asian Games and individual gold at the 2003 Summer Universiade.

name: Emilio Butragueño
milestone: Made his Real Madrid senior debut on 5 February 1984 at age 20, scoring two goals and assisting the third in a 3-2 comeback win over Cádiz; went on to win two consecutive UEFA Cups (1985, 1986) and the Bravo Trophy for best U-24 player in Europe twice.

name: Pau Gasol
milestone: Won the 1998 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship and Albert Schweitzer Tournament with Spain's U-18 team at age 18, then debuted for FC Barcelona's senior team in January 1999 and won two ACB league championships and the Copa del Rey (named MVP) before being drafted 3rd overall in the 2001 NBA Draft and winning NBA Rookie of the Year in 2002 at age 22.

name: Patrick Ewing
milestone: Led Georgetown University to the NCAA national championship in 1984 at age 21 and was named the tournament's Most Outstanding Player; won Olympic gold with the US team at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics; was selected #1 overall in the 1985 NBA Draft and named NBA Rookie of the Year in 1986 at age 24.

name: David Černý
milestone: Received the Special Prize at the Biennale of Kortrijk, Belgium in 1990 at age 22, and gained international notoriety in April 1991 at age 23 by painting a Soviet war memorial tank pink in central Prague — an act of civil disobedience that resulted in brief arrest and became a symbol of post-communist Czech cultural rebellion.

name: Doublelift
milestone: Won his first LCS championship title with Counter Logic Gaming at the 2015 NA LCS Summer Split playoffs at age 22, later winning multiple LCS titles with TSM and Team Liquid before age 26.

name: Dyrus
milestone: Won the 2011 World Cyber Games Grand Finals champion with Chicks Dig Elo at age 19, and won 3 NA LCS titles with Team SoloMid between 2013-2015 before retiring at age 23.

name: Sneaky
milestone: Won the 2013 Summer NA LCS championship with Cloud9 at age 19, and won the 2014 Spring NA LCS with Cloud9, reaching the World Championship semifinals with Cloud9 in 2016.

name: WildTurtle
milestone: Won the 2013 NA LCS Spring Split championship with Team SoloMid at age 18, becoming TSM's starting ADC, and won multiple LCS titles and the IEM World Championship before age 26.

name: Meteos
milestone: Won the 2013 Summer NA LCS championship with Cloud9 at age 20 and the 2014 Spring NA LCS with Cloud9, establishing himself as one of the top junglers in North America.

name: xPeke
milestone: Won the Season 1 League of Legends World Championship with Fnatic at DreamHack in June 2011 at age 19, and won 3 EU LCS titles with Fnatic before founding his own organization Origen in 2015.

name: s1mple
milestone: Won the PGL Major Stockholm 2021 with Natus Vincere at age 24, earning tournament MVP, and was named HLTV Player of the Year in 2018 at age 21, widely considered the greatest CS:GO player of all time.

name: ZywOo
milestone: Named HLTV #1 player of the year in 2019 at age 19, the youngest and second-youngest ever to receive the award, in his first full year as a professional player; won 3 Majors and was named HLTV #1 four times by age 25.

name: NiKo
milestone: Signed by mousesports in March 2015 at age 18 and joined FaZe Clan in February 2017 at age 20, winning multiple premier tournaments including ESL One New York 2017 and EPICENTER 2018, ranked HLTV #2 in 2017, widely considered the best rifler in CS:GO history.

name: dev1ce
milestone: Won the ELEAGUE Major 2017 with Astralis at age 21, the first of 4 CS:GO Major championships; ranked HLTV #3 in 2015 and 2016, and HLTV #2 in 2018, with 9 consecutive HLTV Top 20 appearances.

name: coldzera
milestone: Won the MLG Columbus 2016 Major with Luminosity Gaming at age 21, earning Major MVP, and won ESL One Cologne 2016 Major with SK Gaming; named HLTV #1 player of the year in both 2016 and 2017, becoming the first Brazilian to win a Major MVP.

name: FalleN
milestone: Won the MLG Columbus 2016 Major with Luminosity Gaming at age 24 and the ESL One Cologne 2016 Major with SK Gaming at age 25, becoming a two-time Major champion and the godfather of Brazilian Counter-Strike; named HLTV #2 player of 2016 and Forbes 30 Under 30 in 2017.

name: Stellan Bengtsson
milestone: Won the Men's Singles title at the 1971 World Table Tennis Championships in Nagoya at age 18, becoming the youngest ever men's singles world champion and the first Swede to win the title.

name: Xie Jun
milestone: Won the Women's World Chess Championship in 1991 at age 20, defeating Maia Chiburdanidze who had held the title since 1978; successfully defended the title in 1993.

name: Armada (Adam Lindgren)
milestone: Won his first national Melee tournament (SMASH ATTACK) at age 16 in 2009, became the best player in Europe, and by age 26 had won 3 GENESIS titles, 2 EVO titles, 2 Apex titles, and been ranked the #1 Melee player in the world in 2015 and 2016 as one of the 'Five Gods' of Melee.

name: Mang0 (Joseph Marquez)
milestone: Won his first major tournament (Pound 3) at age 16 in 2008, broke out at EVO World 2007 at 15, and by age 26 had won two EVO titles (2013, 2014), been ranked #1 in the world, and established himself as one of the 'Five Gods' of Melee with over 30 major tournament wins.

name: Mew2King (Jason Zimmerman)
milestone: By age 26, had won 9+ Melee majors and 11+ Brawl majors including 3 MLG championships (2010), was considered the best Melee and Brawl player in the world from 2008-2009, and was one of the 'Five Gods' of Melee; pioneered frame data mining that is still referenced today.

name: Bugha (Kyle Giersdorf)
milestone: Won the Fortnite World Cup 2019 Solo championship at age 16, earning $3 million in the highest-profile esports event of the year; became the highest-earning Fortnite Battle Royale player of all time and won 3x FNCS Champion titles (2021, 2022) by age 23.

name: Clix (Cody Conrod)
milestone: Qualified for the Fortnite World Cup in both solos and duos at age 14 in 2019, earning $175,000; made his first $1 million at age 13; built one of the largest streaming communities in gaming with 8.5M Twitch followers and 3.82M YouTube subscribers by age 20.

name: TenZ (Tyson Ngo)
milestone: Won VCT Stage Two Masters Reykjavik in 2021 at age 20, the first-ever international Valorant LAN, with Sentinels; won VCT Masters Madrid in 2024 at age 23; recognized as one of the faces of competitive Valorant with 4.5M Twitch followers and 2.61M YouTube subscribers.

name: Sinatraa (Jay Won)
milestone: Won Overwatch League 2019 Season 2 Grand Finals championship and was named OWL MVP at age 19; won the 2019 Overwatch World Cup with Team USA and was named tournament MVP; transitioned to Valorant and won the first major international Valorant tournament with Sentinels in 2021 at age 21.

name: Nairo (Nairoby Quezada)
milestone: Won Apex 2014 (super major) at age 17, the largest Brawl tournament, defeating ZeRo; won 10 Smash 4 majors and was ranked 2nd on the PGR100 all-time rankings; broke ZeRo's 56-tournament winning streak at MLG World Finals 2015 at age 18; signed with Team Liquid and NRG Esports.

name: Lil Nas X (Montero Hill)
milestone: Released 'Old Town Road' in December 2018 at age 19, which went viral on TikTok and spent a record 19 weeks at #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 2019; won 2 Grammy Awards in 2020; signed to Columbia Records and released debut album 'Montero' in 2021 with hits 'Industry Baby' and 'Montero (Call Me By Your Name)'.

name: Post Malone (Austin Post)
milestone: Released 'White Iverson' on SoundCloud in February 2015 at age 19, which earned over 4 million streams and led to signing with Republic Records; released debut album 'Stoney' in 2016 with Diamond-certified single 'Congratulations'; by age 26 had multiple #1 Billboard hits and Grammy nominations.

name: Doja Cat (Amala Dlamini)
milestone: Released 'So High' on SoundCloud in 2012 at age 17, catching the attention of Kemosabe and RCA Records; signed a recording contract and released debut EP 'Purrr!' in 2014; 'Mooo!' went viral in August 2018 at age 22; released 'Hot Pink' in 2019 with #1 hit 'Say So'; won Grammy Award in 2022 at age 26.

name: Clairo (Claire Cottrill)
milestone: 'Pretty Girl' went viral on YouTube in 2017 at age 18, reaching 1 million views in a week; signed to Fader Label and released debut EP 'Diary 001' in 2018; released debut album 'Immunity' in 2019 with charting singles 'Bags' and 'Sofia'; Grammy nomination for Best Alternative Music Album in 2025 for self-released 'Charm'.

name: Jan Błachowicz
milestone: Won the KSW 9 light heavyweight tournament on May 9, 2008 at age 25, defeating three opponents in one night to claim the tournament crown in Poland's top MMA promotion.

name: Jannik Sinner
milestone: Won the 2019 Next Gen ATP Finals in Milan at age 18, becoming the youngest champion; also won first Challenger title at 17 and reached Roland Garros quarterfinal and won first ATP title at 19.

name: Andreas Wenzel
milestone: Won the combined event World Championship gold in 1978 at age 20; also won his first World Cup race in March 1978 at age 19 and the overall World Cup title in 1980 at age 22.

name: Kim Yeon-koung
milestone: In the 2005-06 V-League season at age 17, became the first player in Korean professional sports history to win Rookie of the Year, regular league MVP, and championship MVP simultaneously, leading Heungkuk Life to their first championship.

name: Peter Karlsson
milestone: Won World Championship team gold with Sweden in 1989 at age 20, and World Championship men's doubles gold in 1991 at age 22.

name: Cuco
milestone: Signed a seven-figure record deal with Interscope Records in March 2019 at age 20, after accumulating hundreds of millions of streams on YouTube and SoundCloud as an independent artist.

name: Boy Pablo
milestone: His single 'Everytime' went viral via YouTube algorithms in 2017, earning over 10 million plays across streaming platforms and leading to his debut EP Roy Pablo and a sold-out US/Canada club tour by 2018.

name: Rex Orange County
milestone: Featured on three tracks of Tyler, the Creator's critically acclaimed album Flower Boy in July 2017 at age 19, and released his own album Apricot Princess earlier that year, establishing him as a major indie-pop talent.

name: 24kGoldn
milestone: His single 'Valentino' went viral on TikTok in early 2019 at age 18, becoming his first Billboard Hot 100 entry and earning double platinum certification, leading to a major-label deal with Columbia/Records; 'Mood' hit #1 on the Hot 100 in 2020 at age 19.

name: Jack Harlow
milestone: Signed with Generation Now (Atlantic Records imprint) in 2018 at age 20, then 'Whats Poppin' peaked at #2 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 2020 with diamond certification, earning a Grammy nomination.

name: Roddy Ricch
milestone: His single 'Die Young' became his first Billboard Hot 100 entry in 2018 at age 20, and he won a Grammy Award for Best Rap Performance in 2019 at age 21 for 'Racks in the Middle' with Nipsey Hussle, establishing him as a major rap figure.

name: PinkPantheress
milestone: Several of her songs went viral on TikTok in 2021 at age 20, leading to record deals with Parlophone and Elektra Records and the release of her debut mixtape To Hell with It, with 'Just for Me' reaching the UK Top 5.

name: Tate McRae
milestone: Became the first Canadian finalist on So You Think You Can Dance at age 13 in 2016, then her original song 'One Day' went viral on YouTube with 40M+ views in 2017, leading to a RCA Records signing and 'You Broke Me First' reaching the Billboard Hot 100 at age 17.

name: Olivia Rodrigo
milestone: Cast as a lead in Disney Channel's Bizaardvark at age 13 in 2016, then starred in Disney+'s High School Musical: The Musical: The Series in 2019, with her original song 'All I Want' gaining millions of streams; 'Drivers License' hit #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 at age 17 in 2021.

name: Conan Gray
milestone: Signed with Republic Records in 2018 at age 19 after building a YouTube following of 900K+ subscribers, with his viral single 'Idle Town' (2017) and debut EP Sunset Season (2018) establishing him as a rising pop artist.

name: Lauv
milestone: His song 'The Other' went viral on Hype Machine in 2014 at age 20, and 'I Like Me Better' became a worldwide hit in 2017 at age 23 with 75M+ YouTube streams, establishing him as a streaming-era pop breakout.

name: Powfu
milestone: Released 'Death Bed (Coffee for Your Head)' on SoundCloud in February 2019 at age 19, which accumulated 5M SoundCloud plays and 24M YouTube views before being re-released commercially in 2020, hitting #23 on the Billboard Hot 100 and earning a Columbia Records deal.

name: Cavetown (Robin Daniel Skinner)
milestone: Signed to Sire Records in 2019 at age 20 and released major-label debut album Sleepyhead in 2020, building on a YouTube channel with 2.26M subscribers and 612M+ views.

name: Girl in Red (Marie Ulven Ringheim)
milestone: Released debut EP Chapter 1 in September 2018 at age 19, with singles 'Summer Depression' and 'Girls' gaining millions of streams; 'I Wanna Be Your Girlfriend' listed #9 on NYT's Best Songs of 2018.

name: beabadoobee (Beatrice Kristi Ilejay Laus)
milestone: Released 'Coffee' in September 2017 at age 17, gaining 300K+ YouTube views and signing to Dirty Hit Records in April 2018; released five EPs by 2021 and debut album Fake It Flowers in October 2020.

name: Steve Lacy (Steve Thomas Lacy-Moya)
milestone: Joined The Internet in 2015 at age 17 and produced on their Grammy-nominated album Ego Death; released solo EP Steve Lacy's Demo in 2017 and co-produced Kendrick Lamar's 'Pride' on Damn, earning a Grammy nomination for Apollo XXI in 2019.

name: Daniel Caesar (Ashton Dumar Norwill Simmonds)
milestone: Released debut album Freudian in August 2017 at age 22, receiving three Grammy nominations and winning Best R&B Performance for 'Best Part' with H.E.R. at the 61st Grammy Awards.

name: Brent Faiyaz (Christopher Brent Wood)
milestone: Featured on GoldLink's 'Crew' in December 2016 at age 21, which peaked at #45 on the Billboard Hot 100 and was nominated for Best Rap/Sung Performance at the 59th Grammy Awards; released debut album Sonder Son in 2017.

name: Khalid (Khalid Donnel Robinson)
milestone: Released debut single 'Location' in 2016 at age 18, which charted on Billboard and led to signing with RCA; debut album American Teen (March 2017) went 4x platinum and earned Grammy nominations.

name: H.E.R. (Gabriella Sarmiento Wilson)
milestone: Released debut EP H.E.R. Vol. 1 in September 2016 at age 19, with industry co-signs from Usher, Rihanna, and Alicia Keys; self-titled compilation album (2017) won two Grammy Awards including Best R&B Album.

name: Summer Walker
milestone: Released debut commercial mixtape Last Day of Summer in October 2018 at age 22, with 'Girls Need Love' becoming a viral hit; debut album Over It (August 2019) peaked at #2 on Billboard 200 and went triple platinum.

name: Megan Thee Stallion (Megan Jovon Ruth Pete)
milestone: Released SoundCloud mixtapes in 2016-2017 and signed with 1501 Certified Entertainment in 2018; 'Big Ole Freak' became her first Hot 100 entry in 2019 and 'Hot Girl Summer' peaked at #11 in August 2019, creating a cultural phenomenon.

name: Tinashe (Tinashe Jorgensen Kachingwe)
milestone: Joined girl group The Stunners in 2007 at age 14, signed to Columbia Records, and opened for Justin Bieber's My World Tour in 2010; solo breakout '2 On' reached #24 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 2014 and debut album Aquarius was released the same year.

name: Kehlani (Kehlani Ashley Parrish)
milestone: As lead vocalist of PopLyfe, finished fourth on America's Got Talent in 2011 at age 16; released Cloud 19 mixtape in 2014 and You Should Be Here mixtape in 2015, earning a Grammy nomination for Best Urban Contemporary Album and signing to Atlantic Records.

name: Anja Pärson
milestone: Won gold in the giant slalom at the 1998 Junior World Championships at age 17, then won her first World Cup race (a slalom at Mammoth Mountain) in December 1998 at age 17, becoming the fifth Swedish woman to win a World Cup slalom.

name: Chris Benoit
milestone: Won the Stampede British Commonwealth Mid-Heavyweight Championship on March 18, 1988 at age 20, and went on to wrestle for New Japan Pro-Wrestling, winning the IWGP Junior Heavyweight Championship in 1990 at age 23.

name: Smokepurpp
milestone: Signed with Alamo/Interscope Records in March 2017 and released debut mixtape Deadstar which peaked at #42 on the Billboard 200, with lead single 'Audi' earning platinum certification and over 25 million SoundCloud plays.

name: Ski Mask the Slump God
milestone: Released debut studio album Stokeley in November 2018 which peaked at #6 on the Billboard 200, following the platinum-certified singles 'BabyWipe' and 'Take a Step Back' from his 2017 debut commercial mixtape You Will Regret.

name: XXXTentacion
milestone: Released debut album 17 (2017) peaking at #2 on Billboard 200 and second album ? (2018) debuting at #1, both certified triple platinum; single 'Sad!' posthumously reached #1 on Billboard Hot 100 with diamond certification. Died at age 20 in June 2018.

name: Juice WRLD
milestone: Released diamond-certified single 'Lucid Dreams' which peaked at #2 on Billboard Hot 100 in 2018, debut album Goodbye & Good Riddance (triple platinum), and second album Death Race for Love which debuted at #1 on Billboard 200 in 2019. Died at age 21 in December 2019.

name: Lil Peep
milestone: Pioneered the emo-rap genre with widely acclaimed SoundCloud mixtapes Crybaby and Hellboy (2016) and released debut studio album Come Over When You're Sober, Pt. 1 in August 2017, building a massive cult following. Died at age 21 in November 2017.

name: Trippie Redd
milestone: Released debut mixtape A Love Letter to You in 2017 via 10K Projects which entered the Billboard 200, with lead single 'Love Scars' earning double platinum certification; followed by debut album Life's a Trip in 2018.

name: Polo G
milestone: Released debut album Die a Legend in June 2019 which peaked at #6 on Billboard 200 and was certified double platinum, preceded by 'Pop Out' featuring Lil Tjay which peaked at #11 on the Hot 100 with over 200 million YouTube views. Third album Hall of Fame (2021) became his first #1 album with single 'Rapstar' reaching #1 on Hot 100.

name: NLE Choppa
milestone: Released breakout single 'Shotta Flow' in January 2019 at age 16 which earned platinum certification, peaked at #36 on the Billboard Hot 100, and garnered 10 million YouTube views in a month; sparked a $3 million label bidding war and led to debut EP Cottonwood and debut album Top Shotta (2020) reaching top 10 on Billboard 200.

name: Baby Keem
milestone: Won Grammy Award for Best Rap Performance for 'Family Ties' with Kendrick Lamar at the 64th Grammy Awards in 2022; debut studio album The Melodic Blue (2021) peaked at #5 on Billboard 200 and was certified platinum; contributed to Black Panther soundtrack (2018) and Beyoncé's The Lion King: The Gift (2019) as a producer.

name: Yeat
milestone: Achieved viral success on TikTok in mid-2021 with mixtape 4L and debut album Up 2 Me, with tracks 'Money So Big' and 'Get Busy' gaining considerable popularity; second album 2 Alive (2022) debuted in Billboard 200 top ten, establishing him as a leading figure in the rage microgenre.

name: Playboi Carti
milestone: Released self-titled debut mixtape in 2017 peaking at #12 on Billboard 200 with singles 'Magnolia' and 'Wokeuplikethis', followed by debut studio album Die Lit in 2018 debuting at #3 on Billboard 200. Founded the Opium record label/collective in 2019.

name: Lil Uzi Vert
milestone: Released debut studio album Luv Is Rage 2 in 2017 which debuted at #1 on Billboard 200 and was certified double platinum, preceded by 'XO Tour Llif3' which won MTV VMA Song of Summer and became one of the most streamed songs of 2017; featured on Migos' 'Bad and Boujee' which hit #1 on Hot 100 in 2016; Grammy nomination for Best New Artist in 2018.

name: Jorja Smith
milestone: Featured twice on Drake's chart-topping 'More Life' playlist in March 2017 at age 19, after her independently released single 'Blue Lights' went viral and she placed on the BBC Sound of 2017 list.

name: Ella Mai
milestone: Her single 'Boo'd Up' became a sleeper hit in 2018, peaking at #5 on the Billboard Hot 100 and winning the Grammy for Best R&B Song, while her debut album reached #5 on the Billboard 200.

name: Normani
milestone: As a member of Fifth Harmony, one of the best-selling girl groups of all time, she achieved multiplatinum hits and arena tours starting at age 16; her solo single 'Love Lies' with Khalid reached #9 on the Hot 100 at age 22.

name: Camila Cabello
milestone: As a member of Fifth Harmony from age 15, she achieved global fame with multiplatinum hits; her solo single 'Havana' reached #1 on the Hot 100 and her debut album topped the Billboard 200 at age 20.

name: Dua Lipa
milestone: Released her debut single 'New Love' at age 20 in 2015, followed by debut album 'Dua Lipa' in 2017 with the massive hit 'New Rules,' and won the Grammy for Best New Artist in 2019 at age 23.

name: Ava Max
milestone: Her debut single 'Sweet but Psycho' was released in August 2018 at age 24, hitting #1 in 22 countries and #10 on the Billboard Hot 100, becoming one of the biggest pop hits of 2019.

name: Kim Petras
milestone: Released her debut single 'I Don't Want It at All' in August 2017 at age 24, which charted on Spotify's Global Viral Chart, followed by multiple singles that charted on Billboard's Dance/Electronic Songs chart before age 26.

name: Troye Sivan
milestone: Released his debut EP 'TRXYE' in August 2014 at age 19, which debuted at #5 on the Billboard 200, leveraging his 3M+ YouTube subscriber base built from six years of vlogging and singing.

name: Joji
milestone: As Filthy Frank/Pink Guy, he built a YouTube following of 5.5M+ subscribers and sparked the viral Harlem Shake meme in 2013 at age 19, then transitioned to music as Joji with the 'In Tongues' EP in 2017 at age 24.

name: DDG
milestone: Signed to Epic Records in 2018 at age 20 after building millions of YouTube subscribers, with his 'Take Me Serious' mixtape and singles like 'Run It Up' establishing him as a YouTube-to-music crossover artist.

name: 6ix9ine
milestone: Released debut single 'Gummo' in September 2017 at age 21, which peaked at #12 on the Billboard Hot 100, followed by 'Day69' mixtape debuting at #4 on the Billboard 200 and 'Fefe' reaching #3 in 2018.

name: Lil Pump
milestone: Released 'Gucci Gang' in August 2017 at age 17, which peaked at #3 on the Billboard Hot 100 and was certified 5x platinum, preceded by his self-titled debut album that reached #3 on the Billboard 200.

name: Kang Jae-won
milestone: Won gold medal with South Korea at the 1986 Asian Games in Seoul at age 21, and later Olympic silver at the 1988 Seoul Olympics at age 23; named IHF World Player of the Year in 1989 at age 24.

name: Arturo Gatti
milestone: Won the IBF junior lightweight world championship on December 15, 1995 at age 23, defeating Tracy Harris Patterson at Madison Square Garden.

name: Dolph Lundgren
milestone: Won the European Kyokushin Karate Heavyweight Championship in 1980 at age 23 and retained the title in 1981; also won the Australian Kyokushinkai Full-Contact Karate Tournament in 1982.

name: Daniel Day-Lewis
milestone: Took over the lead role in the West End play 'Another Country' in late 1982 at age 25, and appeared in the film 'Gandhi' (1982); joined the Royal Shakespeare Company in 1983 at age 26, playing Romeo in Romeo and Juliet.

name: Shaquille O'Neal
milestone: Named AP Player of the Year and First-team All-American as a sophomore at LSU in 1990-91 at age 18-19; selected as the #1 overall pick in the 1992 NBA draft at age 20; won NBA Rookie of the Year in 1992-93 at age 20-21.

name: 21 Savage
milestone: Released the collaborative EP Savage Mode with Metro Boomin in July 2016, peaking at #23 on the Billboard 200, and followed with debut album Issa Album (2017) debuting at #2 on the Billboard 200 with single 'Bank Account' reaching #33 on the Hot 100.

name: Gunna
milestone: Signed to Young Thug's YSL Records in 2016, released the Drip Season mixtape series (2016-2018), and the collaborative mixtape Drip Harder with Lil Baby (2018) peaked at #4 on the Billboard 200 with single 'Drip Too Hard' reaching #4 on the Hot 100 and earning diamond certification.

name: Lil Baby
milestone: Released four mixtapes in 2017 including Harder than Hard (which spawned first Hot 100 entry 'My Dawg'), signed to Quality Control Music, and released debut album Harder Than Ever (2018) peaking at #3 on the Billboard 200 with top-10 single 'Yes Indeed' featuring Drake.

name: Yung Lean
milestone: The music video for 'Ginseng Strip 2002' went viral on YouTube in 2013 at age 16, leading to international recognition; released debut mixtape Unknown Death 2002 (2013) and debut album Unknown Memory (2014), establishing the cloud rap / SoundCloud rap aesthetic.

name: Bladee
milestone: Formed the Drain Gang collective in 2013, released debut mixtape Gluee (2014) and debut album Eversince (2016), and collaborated extensively with Yung Lean, building a significant internet cult following across multiple projects by age 26.

name: Sheck Wes
milestone: Released 'Mo Bamba' in 2017 which went viral and peaked at #6 on the Billboard Hot 100; signed to Travis Scott's Cactus Jack and Kanye West's GOOD Music in a joint venture with Interscope Records in February 2018; released debut album Mudboy (October 2018) and guested on Travis Scott's Astroworld.

name: Arlo Parks
milestone: Released debut album Collapsed in Sunbeams (January 2021) at age 20, peaking at #3 on the UK Albums Chart and winning the 2021 Mercury Prize; also nominated for Best New Artist and Best British Female at the Brit Awards and Best Alternative Music Album at the Grammys.

name: Declan McKenna
milestone: Won the Glastonbury Festival Emerging Talent Competition in April 2015 at age 16, self-released 'Brazil' which went viral on YouTube and reached #16 on the Billboard Alternative Songs chart, signed to Columbia Records in 2015, and released debut album What Do You Think About the Car? in 2017.

name: Omar Apollo
milestone: Released debut album Ivory (2022) to positive reviews and earned a Grammy Award nomination for Best New Artist at the 65th Annual Grammy Awards (announced November 2022), all before age 26; earlier milestones include breakout single 'Ugotme' (2017), debut EP Stereo (2018), and debut mixtape Apolonio (2020).

name: SZA
milestone: Self-released debut EP See.SZA.Run (October 2012), signed to Top Dawg Entertainment in July 2013 as the label's first female artist, released EP Z (2014) to critical attention, and wrote for major artists including Beyoncé and Rihanna — all before age 26.

name: Madison Beer
milestone: Justin Bieber tweeted her YouTube cover of 'At Last' to 25 million followers in July 2012 at age 13, leading to signing with Island Records and management by Scooter Braun in 2013; released debut single 'Melodies' (2013), debut EP As She Pleases (2018), debut album Life Support (2021) with RIAA Platinum single 'Selfish', and second album Silence Between Songs (2023) with a Grammy nomination — all before age 26.

name: Vreni Schneider
milestone: Won her first World Cup race in December 1984 at age 20, and by age 26 had won two Olympic gold medals (1988 Calgary), two World Championship golds (1987, 1989), and set a single-season record of 14 World Cup wins in 1988-89.

name: Stoya
milestone: Won AVN Best New Starlet award in January 2009 at age 22 and signed an exclusive three-year contract with Digital Playground in October 2007, making her the company's first alt-porn contract star.

name: Tori Black
milestone: Won AVN Female Performer of the Year in 2010 at age 22 and again in 2011 at age 23, becoming the first person in history to win the award back-to-back; was also Penthouse Pet of the Month in December 2008.

name: Asa Akira
milestone: By age 26 in 2012, she had appeared in over 300 adult films since starting in 2006, was a regular on the Bubba the Love Sponge radio show, and had established herself as one of the most popular and prolific performers in the industry, later winning AVN Female Performer of the Year in 2013.

name: Bree Olson
milestone: Entered the adult film industry in November 2006 at age 20, became Penthouse Pet of the Month in March 2008, signed as contract performer with Adam & Eve from 2007 to 2010, and was named one of the top 12 female porn stars by Maxim in 2010 at age 24.

name: Dani Daniels
milestone: By age 26 in 2015, she was a four-year veteran of the adult industry with over 600 film credits, named one of porn's biggest stars by CNBC, and won XBIZ Female Performer of the Year in January 2016 at age 26.

name: Christy Mack
milestone: By age 21 in 2012, she had entered the adult industry in 2011, appeared in the Dark Knight XXX porn parody as Zatanna, launched her official website in April 2013, and became a Fleshlight Girl with signature products released in November 2013, establishing herself as a major tattoo-icon performer.

name: Bonnie Rotten
milestone: Won AVN Female Performer of the Year in 2014 at age 21, becoming the first alt-porn star to win the award; also nominated for AVN and XRCO Best New Starlet in 2013 and founded her own production company Mental Beauty, Inc.

name: Alex Cooper
milestone: Co-created Call Her Daddy podcast in 2018 at age 24; within two months downloads surged from 12,000 to 2 million per episode, and by 2020 at age 26 it was the 5th most popular podcast on Spotify, making her one of the most successful female podcasters in the world.

name: Cody Ko
milestone: Created the I'd Cap That iOS app in 2012 at age 22, which went viral with over 4 million users and became the App Store's #1 free app, then was acquired for low six-figures; subsequently built ~2 million followers on Vine before transitioning to YouTube.

name: Noel Miller
milestone: Built a following of 100,000+ on Vine by 2014-2015 through comedy skits, with one viral video garnering 2.6 million loops, and launched his YouTube channel in August 2015 at age 26, beginning the transition that would lead to major online comedy success.

name: Danny Gonzalez
milestone: Gained prominence on Vine in 2014 at age 20 with viral comedy sketches, then successfully transitioned to YouTube in 2017, building millions of subscribers and billions of views by age 26 in 2020.

name: Drew Gooden
milestone: Built 400,000+ followers on Vine by 2016 with viral content including the iconic 'Road Work Ahead' Vine (one of the most viral Vines of all time), then successfully transitioned to YouTube in 2016-2017, gaining 100,000 subscribers in just two weeks and building millions of subscribers by age 26 in 2019.

name: Miquel Barceló
milestone: Participated as the only Spanish artist in Documenta 7 in Kassel, Germany, in 1982 at age 25, gaining international recognition.

milestone: Founded WHOOP in 2012 at age 22 while a Harvard undergraduate and squash captain, building wearable technology focused on recovery and strain rather than step counting; first devices launched 2015.

name: Chris Cox
milestone: Joined Facebook in 2005 at age 22–23 as one of the company's first ~15 software engineers after dropping out of a Stanford Symbolic Systems graduate program; helped build News Feed, a defining product surface.

name: Niki Parmar
milestone: Joined Google in 2015 at age 24 as a software engineer on Google Brain—the youngest member of her team and the only one without a PhD—and by 2017 (age ~26) was an equal co-author of the seminal NeurIPS paper 'Attention Is All You Need' that introduced the Transformer architecture.

name: Gabe Newell
milestone: Dropped out of Harvard and joined Microsoft in 1983 at age 20–21 (about the 271st employee), then produced the first major releases of the Windows operating system (Windows 1.0 in 1985 at age 22–23; Windows 2.0 in 1987 at age 24–25), a material early contribution to mainstream PC software.

name: Kimbal Musk
milestone: Co-founded Zip2 (initially Global Link Information Network) with brother Elon Musk and Greg Kouri in 1995 at age 22–23, building online city-guide software for newspapers; the company sold to Compaq for about $307 million in 1999 when Kimbal was 26–27.

name: Aditya Agarwal
milestone: Joined Facebook in summer 2005 as one of its first engineers (age ~22–23), built the platform's early search engine at Mark Zuckerberg's direction, and by age 24 was managing engineers, later becoming Facebook's first Director of Product Engineering.

name: Alec Radford
milestone: Lead author of OpenAI's 2018 generative pre-training paper introducing GPT (foundational to ChatGPT) at age 25, after joining OpenAI around 2016 at age ~23 and co-founding AI startup Indico while at Olin College.

name: Joseph J. Allaire
milestone: Created ColdFusion and co-founded Allaire Corporation with brother Jeremy in May 1995 at age 25, launching a pioneering web application server and company that later IPO'd (1999) and was acquired by Macromedia (2001).

name: Paul Buchheit
milestone: Created Gmail at Google and launched it publicly on April 1, 2004 at age 26 (born Nov 7, 1977); as Google employee #23 he had begun the project around 2001 and also prototyped what became AdSense and popularized the “Don’t be evil” motto.

name: Chandrajit Bajaj
milestone: Completed a Cornell PhD in computer science in 1984 under John E. Hopcroft (after a 1983 master’s) and began a Purdue University computer science faculty position the same year, at approximately age 26 (born 1958; BTech IIT Delhi 1980).

name: Matt Cohler
milestone: Joined LinkedIn’s founding team in 2003 as vice president and general manager (LinkedIn launched May 2003) at age 25–26 (born March 27, 1977), becoming CEO Reid Hoffman’s early operational right hand after McKinsey and China work.

name: Nikolai Mushegian
milestone: Co-founded MakerDAO with Rune Christensen around 2015 (age 21–22; born March 28, 1993) and designed/built the Single-Collateral Dai stablecoin system that launched in December 2017 when he was 24.

name: Serafina Brocious
milestone: At age 17 (2005), as high-school student Cody Brocious, co-created PyMusique with Jon Lech Johansen, a Linux client for the iTunes Music Store that purchased songs without FairPlay DRM—covered nationally by Forbes and NBC News.

name: Gregory Abowd
milestone: Selected as a Rhodes Scholar after graduating summa cum laude in honors mathematics from Notre Dame (1986, age 21–22) and completed an Oxford M.Sc. in Computation in 1987 at age 22–23; D.Phil. followed in 1991 (age 26–27).

name: Caroline Ellison
milestone: Joined Alameda Research as a trader in March 2018 at age 23 after Jane Street; by October 2021 (still age 26, born November 1994) became co-CEO of Alameda Research, the major crypto trading firm affiliated with FTX.

name: Do Kwon
milestone: Co-founded Terraform Labs in January 2018 with Daniel Shin, launching the Terra blockchain and later the Luna/UST ecosystem that reached multi-billion market cap before collapsing in 2022.

name: Feross Aboukhadijeh
milestone: Built and launched YouTube Instant in September 2010 at age 19 while a Stanford student and Facebook intern; the site went viral (hundreds of thousands to 1M+ visitors) and drew a public job offer from YouTube CEO Chad Hurley.

name: Hugo Barra
milestone: Co-founded mobile software startup Lobby7 in 1999 with MIT classmates and SoftBank investment at age ~22–23; the company was acquired by ScanSoft (later Nuance) in 2003.

name: Łukasz Kaiser
milestone: Completed a Ph.D. in computer science at RWTH Aachen University on 2 October 2008 (age 26) with the dissertation Logic and Games on Automatic Structures; the dissertation later received the 2009 E.W. Beth Dissertation Prize for outstanding work in logic, language, and information.

name: Solomon Hykes
milestone: Co-founded dotCloud (the company that later became Docker, Inc.) in 2008 in Paris/Montrouge with Sebastien Pahl, building a multi-language PaaS that would pivot into the Docker container project.

name: Edward Coristine
milestone: Appointed in early 2025 (age 19) as one of the youngest engineers on Elon Musk's Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), with subsequent roles across GSA, State, DHS/CISA, and Social Security Administration systems access.

name: Biz Stone
milestone: Helped form and served as creative director of Xanga (1999–2001), an early blogging/social journaling platform, at age 25–27—his first material product leadership role in consumer internet media.

name: Near (programmer)
milestone: Launched the bsnes project on October 14, 2004 (age 21), building the first Super Nintendo emulator to pursue and later achieve 100% library compatibility through cycle-accurate hardware emulation; earlier completed Dragon Quest V fan translation in November 2001 (age 18).

name: Alfred Lutter
milestone: At age 12 starred as Tommy opposite Ellen Burstyn in Martin Scorsese’s Alice Doesn't Live Here Anymore (1974), earning a BAFTA nomination for Most Promising Newcomer; followed with roles in Love and Death (1975) and The Bad News Bears (1976) before age 15.

name: H. D. Moore
milestone: Founded the Metasploit Project in summer 2003 at about age 22, creating an open-source penetration-testing framework that became the industry-standard exploit development and testing platform.

name: Bob Lee
milestone: Joined Google as a staff software engineer in October 2004 at age 24, contributing to Android and core Java libraries; by age 26 co-created the Guice dependency-injection framework (2006).

name: Ezra Callahan
milestone: Joined Facebook in December 2004 at about age 23 as one of the first ~20 employees and the company's first product manager, hired by Sean Parker during the Los Altos house era.

name: Terri Burns
milestone: In October 2020, at age 26, promoted to investing partner at GV (Google Ventures)—the firm's youngest partner and first Black woman partner—after joining as principal in 2017.

name: Duane Chase
milestone: At age 14 (film released 1965; cast/filmed at 13–14), played Kurt von Trapp in The Sound of Music, one of the most commercially successful and culturally enduring films of the 20th century.

name: Randi Zuckerberg
milestone: In 2005, at age 23, was recruited by brother Mark Zuckerberg and joined Facebook as one of the first ~10 employees, later serving as director of market development and company spokesperson.

name: Pete Hunt
milestone: As an early React team member at Facebook/Instagram, helped take React from an internal experimental UI library to a public open-source release (JSConf US, May 2013) and became its primary external evangelist through conference talks that reversed initial community hostility.

name: Mislav Marohnić
milestone: By about 2007 (age ~21) he was already the primary author/maintainer of will_paginate, a widely adopted Rails pagination library, and by ~2010 (age ~24) he created and began long-term maintenance of hub, the popular GitHub-oriented git CLI wrapper.

name: Parisa Tabriz
milestone: Co-authored a USENIX Security Symposium paper on 802.11 device driver fingerprinting in 2006 at about age 23, then joined Google's security team as an information security engineer in 2007 at about age 24 after B.S./M.S. degrees at UIUC.

name: Kyle Davies
milestone: Co-founded Three Arrows Capital (3AC) with Su Zhu in 2012 at about age 25, after Phillips Academy, Columbia, and a Credit Suisse trading stint; the fund later became one of the largest crypto hedge funds before its 2022 collapse.

name: Chris Espinosa
milestone: Joined Apple Computer in 1976 at age 14 as employee number 8 while the company still operated from Steve Jobs's parents' garage, writing BASIC programs, documentation, and demonstrating the Apple I after school.

name: Patrick Baynes
milestone: Co-founded PeopleLinx in 2009 at age 24–25 after joining LinkedIn in 2007 as an early employee (#162), building a B2B social selling/SaaS company that later raised venture capital and served Fortune 500 clients.

name: Nathan Adams
milestone: Hired by Mojang Studios on February 28, 2012 (age 20) as a Minecraft developer focused on the mod API, after co-creating the widely used Bukkit plugin platform and working at Curse.

name: Tobias Lütke
milestone: In 2004 co-launched Snowdevil, an online snowboard shop built on a custom Ruby on Rails e-commerce stack that the founders soon productized and relaunched as Shopify in 2006 (still at or under age 26).

name: Scott Farquhar
milestone: Co-founded Atlassian in 2002 with Mike Cannon-Brookes shortly after university, bootstrapping with credit-card debt and shipping Jira as a self-serve product.

name: Mike Cannon-Brookes
milestone: Co-founded Atlassian in 2002 at about age 22 with Scott Farquhar after graduating UNSW; earlier sold student startup The Bookmark Box (2000).

name: Elizabeth Holmes
milestone: Founded Theranos (initially Real-Time Cures) in 2003 at age 19 while at Stanford, filed early patent applications, dropped out in 2004, and raised multi-million seed capital by late 2004.

name: Ryan Hoover
milestone: Launched Product Hunt on November 6, 2013 (initially an email list via Linkydink) while Director of Product at PlayHaven; it rapidly became a central tech product-discovery community and entered YC in 2014.

name: Eoghan McCabe
milestone: Began building Intercom in late 2010/early 2011 at age ~26 (self-reported) after selling prior product Exceptional in 2011; Intercom formally launched with cofounders Des Traynor, Ciaran Lee, and David Barrett in 2011.

name: Mathilde Collin
milestone: Co-founded Front in 2013 (about age 24) with Laurent Perrin, building a shared inbox/customer communication platform; company later became a unicorn.

name: Cliff Obrecht
milestone: Co-founded Fusion Books in 2007 with Melanie Perkins, an online yearbook design platform that became the largest yearbook company in Australia and New Zealand and validated the product thesis later scaled into Canva.

name: Vlad Tenev
milestone: Co-founded Robinhood in 2012–2013 with Baiju Bhatt to offer commission-free stock trading, after earlier fintech startups Celeris (2010) and Chronos Research (2011).

name: Andrew Ng
milestone: Co-authored the seminal Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) paper with David Blei and Michael I. Jordan, presented at NIPS 2001 (age 25), and received his Berkeley PhD under Jordan before joining Stanford as assistant professor in 2002 (age 26).

name: Andy Fang
milestone: Co-founded DoorDash in 2013 at age ~21 while a Stanford computer-science student and served as founding CTO (2013–2019), building the core logistics platform that later IPO'd and made him a billionaire.

name: Stanley Tang
milestone: Co-founded DoorDash in 2013 at age ~20–21 while at Stanford; earlier published Amazon bestseller eMillions: Behind-the-Scenes Stories of 14 Successful Internet Millionaires at age 15–16 (~2008).

name: Leah Culver
milestone: In June 2007, co-founded microblogging/social network Pownce with Digg cofounder Kevin Rose and Daniel Burka, serving as cofounder and lead developer; the product became a high-profile Web 2.0 peer of Twitter and was acquired by Six Apart in late 2008.

name: Mitchell Hashimoto
milestone: Created and open-sourced Vagrant (first public release ~2010), which became a widely adopted tool for portable developer environments and made him well known in DevOps by about age 22–23; founded HashiCorp in mid-2012 at about age 24 to commercialize infrastructure automation tools.

name: Armon Dadgar
milestone: Joined Mitchell Hashimoto as cofounder of HashiCorp in July 2013 (about age 24), helping build the open-source infrastructure automation company that later produced Consul, Terraform, Vault, and related products and became a major DevOps vendor.

name: Zhang Yiming
milestone: In 2009, at age 26, founded 99fang.com by taking over Kuxun's real-estate search business as Expedia prepared to acquire Kuxun's travel unit—his first company as founder/CEO—after earlier roles as Kuxun's first engineer (2006) and brief stints at Microsoft and Fanfou.

name: Jared Friedman
milestone: Co-founded Scribd and entered Y Combinator's summer 2006 batch at about age 22; the company launched publicly in March 2007 and became a leading document-sharing and later subscription reading platform.

name: Andrew Bosworth
milestone: Joined Facebook in January 2006 as roughly the 10th–15th engineer at age 24 and was a principal builder of the original News Feed, which launched later in 2006 and became the product pattern for modern social feeds.

name: Gavin Kliger
milestone: In early 2025 at age ~25, appointed as a high-profile Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) engineer with operational authority across multiple federal agencies after rising to senior software engineer at Databricks with reported seven-figure compensation.

name: Martín Abadi
milestone: Earned a Ph.D. in computer science from Stanford University in 1987 at about age 24 under Zohar Manna, with dissertation Temporal Theorem Proving, establishing an early research career that later produced BAN logic and foundational security work.

name: Lennart Poettering
milestone: Created and first released PulseAudio (initially as Polypaudio) on 17 July 2004 at age 23; the sound server became the default audio stack on major Linux distributions.

name: Olivier Chapelle
milestone: Published the highly cited Machine Learning journal paper “Choosing Multiple Parameters for Support Vector Machines” (with Vapnik, Bousquet, and Mukherjee; ~2002, age ~24) and earlier NIPS 2000 work on Vicinal Risk Minimization; defended PhD on SVMs at Université Pierre et Marie Curie / LIP6 in 2004 (age ~26).

name: Matt Corallo
milestone: Began contributing to Bitcoin Core in early 2011 while still in high school (~age 18), becoming one of the earliest active post-Satoshi Core developers; implemented wallet private-key encryption merged mid-2011 (PRs #232/#352).

name: Alex Smola
milestone: Completed Diplomarbeit (master's thesis) 'Regression Estimation with Support Vector Learning Machines' at TU Munich in 1996 after working with Vladimir Vapnik at AT&T Bell Labs (1995–96), an early foundational contribution to support vector regression; age ~24–25.

name: Dalton Caldwell
milestone: Co-founded imeem in late 2003 (age 23) with Stanford classmate Jan Jannink; the social music platform later raised substantial VC and was acquired by MySpace in 2009.

name: Gagan Biyani
milestone: Co-founded Udemy in 2010 (age 22–23) with Eren Bali and Oktay Caglar; raised seed funding and built an early MOOC marketplace later worth billions.

name: Sam Bankman-Fried
milestone: Co-founded Alameda Research, a quantitative cryptocurrency trading firm, in November 2017 at age 25; the firm rapidly became a major crypto market maker before FTX (founded 2019 at age 27).

name: JB Straubel
milestone: Built an electric Porsche that set a 240 V SC/B world electric-vehicle racing record in 2000 at age 24; earned Stanford MS in energy engineering the same year after a self-designed BS energy systems major.

name: Chelsea Voss
milestone: Won International Biology Olympiad gold medals (3rd place overall 2010; 4th place 2011) representing the U.S. while in high school (~age 17–18); also Intel Science Talent Search national finalist (2011).

name: Alan Cooper
