milestone: In 1975 at age 22–23, founded Structured Systems Group (SSG) in Oakland and shipped General Ledger, widely cited as among the first serious business software packages for microcomputers.

name: Charles Best
milestone: In 2000 at about age 24, founded DonorsChoose while teaching history at a Bronx public high school, creating an early education crowdfunding platform for classroom project requests.

name: Garry Tan
milestone: In September 2005 at about age 24, joined Palantir Technologies as employee #10, designing the company logo and cofounding early product/engineering work on its quant finance analysis platform.

name: Dave Morin
milestone: As Facebook senior platform manager, co-created Facebook Platform (public launch May 2007) enabling third-party apps inside Facebook, at age 26.

name: Michael Baum (entrepreneur)
milestone: Co-founded Reality Online (stock-market modeling software) around Drexel graduation in 1985 at age ~23; the company was Venrock-backed and later acquired by Reuters (sources cite 1987–1989).

name: Naomi Gleit
milestone: Joined Facebook on July 18, 2005 (her 22nd birthday) as employee #29 shortly after the company hit 1 million users; wrote her Stanford senior thesis on Facebook and became a core early growth product leader.

name: Slava Akhmechet
milestone: Co-founded RethinkDB and joined Y Combinator (S09) in May 2009 at about age 26 (born Ukraine; moved to NYC at ~13 in 1996), dropping out of a Stony Brook computational neuroscience PhD to build a distributed database startup.

name: John Resig
milestone: Publicly released jQuery at BarCamp NYC in January 2006 at age 21; it became the most widely used JavaScript library.

name: Bruce Artwick
milestone: Founded Sublogic in October 1977 at age 24 after a 1976 master's thesis demonstrating real-time computer-generated flight display; released the first consumer Flight Simulator for Apple II around 1979–early 1980 (age 26–27).

name: Bret Taylor
milestone: Led the Google team that co-created Google Maps (predecessors Search by Location / Google Local), with Maps launching publicly in February 2005 when he was about 24–25.

name: Pedro Franceschi
milestone: Co-founded Brex in January 2017 at about age 20–21 (after selling teenage payments company Pagar.me), entering Y Combinator and building a multi-billion-dollar corporate card platform well before age 26.

name: Randal Bryant
milestone: In November 1977 at age 25, published his MIT master's thesis Simulation of Packet Communication Architecture Computer Systems (MIT-LCS-TR-188), widely cited as among the first published work on fully distributed discrete-event simulation and a foundation of the Chandy/Misra/Bryant (CMB) algorithm.

name: Elizabeth Bradley
milestone: In 1986 at age 25, competed for the United States at the World Rowing Championships, placing fourth in the women's eight; followed in 1987 (age 26) with a fourth-place finish in women's pairs—material international elite athletic milestones before age 27.

name: Tom Hall
milestone: Lead designer on Commander Keen (first episode released as shareware Dec 14, 1990) and co-founded id Software on February 1, 1991 at age 26 with John Carmack, John Romero, and Adrian Carmack.

name: Kang-Xing Jin
milestone: After graduating Harvard CS in 2006 (same cohort as Mark Zuckerberg; HS Blair Magnet 2002 implies birth ~1984), joined Facebook as an early engineer on the News Feed team and was among the first ~30 Facebook users—material early-product engineering role at age ~22.

name: Brett Harrison
milestone: Published peer-reviewed mathematics research in The American Mathematical Monthly (2007) at age ~19 after RSI at MIT; by 2010 (age 22) joined Jane Street Capital as an ADR trader and later led algorithmic trading systems development.

name: J Allard
milestone: On January 25, 1994, at age 25, wrote the widely cited internal Microsoft memo 'Windows: The Next Killer Application on the Internet,' which helped drive Microsoft’s Internet strategy; already a program manager shipping LAN Manager/TCP-IP stack work after joining Microsoft from Boston University in 1991 (age 22).

name: Fadi Chehadé
milestone: In 1987 at age ~25, founded Nett Information Products (aka Connectica), an Internet-based content management company later acquired by Ingram Micro, after BS CS (NYU Poly 1985) and MS engineering management (Stanford 1986).

name: Michael Pryor
milestone: Co-founded Fog Creek Software with Joel Spolsky in September 2000 in New York City at about age 25, building a developer-centric product company (FogBugz and later Trello lineage) after working as a programmer at Juno.

name: Shin Hyun-seong
milestone: In May 2010 at age 24, co-founded Ticket Monster (TMON), a South Korean Groupon-style mobile e-commerce company that scaled to tens of millions in monthly revenue within roughly a year and later sold to LivingSocial/Groupon.

name: Jaime Carbonell
milestone: In 1979 at age 25–26, completed a Yale PhD under Roger Schank (thesis Subjective Understanding: Computer Models of Belief Systems) and joined Carnegie Mellon University as assistant professor of computer science, launching a top-tier AI/NLP academic career.

name: Andy Baio
milestone: In 2003 at age 26, launched Upcoming.org, a collaborative social event calendar that received New York Times coverage that year and was acquired by Yahoo for about $2 million in 2005.

name: Markus Persson
milestone: By ~2003 at age 23–24, co-founded development of Wurm Online (public alpha 2003; commercial release 2006) with Rolf Jansson via Mojang Specifications—his first shipped commercial MMO sandbox game before Minecraft.

name: Greg Gianforte
milestone: In 1986 at age ~24–25, co-founded Brightwork Development Inc. (LAN management software) in New Jersey after leaving Bell Labs; served as president for eight years until a ~$10M McAfee sale in 1994.

name: Scott Chacon
milestone: In 2007–2008 at age ~25–26, co-founded GitHub with Tom Preston-Werner, Chris Wanstrath, and P.J. Hyett; platform development began Oct 2007 and launched 2008, establishing him as a core founding engineer/operator of the dominant Git hosting company.

name: Geert Uytterhoeven
milestone: By 1994 at age ~23, was an active Linux/m68k kernel hacker (Amiga port lineage—the first non-Intel Linux port), running linux-m68k.org-era work, meeting Linus Torvalds at a Belgian conference, and contributing patches recognized in the kernel community.

name: Jacob Appelbaum
milestone: In 2008 (age 25), co-authored the USENIX Security Best Student Paper cold-boot attack paper (“Lest We Remember”) with Halderman, Felten, and others, also winning a Pwnie Award for Most Innovative Research.

name: Guillaume Lample
milestone: In March 2016 at age 25, first-authored the NAACL 2016 paper Neural Architectures for Named Entity Recognition (BiLSTM-CRF NER), a highly cited SOTA result while at Carnegie Mellon.

name: Hans Peter Brondmo
milestone: In 1987 at about age 24–25, after MIT undergrad, co-founded Snappy Software (expert systems) with seed funding from Apple Computer; by 1988 (age 26) joined Apple on HyperCard development in Japan.

name: Jarvis Johnson
milestone: In August 2018 at age 26, his 5-Minute Crafts commentary video became the breakout that scaled his YouTube channel into full-time creator career after Georgia Tech CS and SWE roles at Google/Yelp/Patreon.

name: Chris Lattner
milestone: Designed and began implementing LLVM with Vikram Adve after joining UIUC in late 2000 (~age 22); completed the LLVM multi-stage optimization M.S. thesis in December 2002 at age ~24, establishing the compiler infrastructure that later became industry-standard.

name: Sean Egan
milestone: Became maintainer of Gaim/Pidgin (major multi-protocol open-source IM client) in early 2002 at age ~19–20 after contributing since 2000; hired by Google onto Google Talk in September 2005 at age 23 and published a technical book on Gaim development the same year.

name: Ben Gordon
milestone: Selected 3rd overall in the 2004 NBA Draft by the Chicago Bulls at age 21 after leading UConn to the 2004 NCAA championship; as a rookie (age 21–22) became the first player to win NBA Sixth Man of the Year as a rookie and made the All-Rookie First Team.

name: Craig Silverstein
milestone: Joined Google in 1998 as its first hire (employee #1 after founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin) at about age 25–26 while a Stanford Ph.D. student, becoming a core systems/search engineer and later director of technology.

name: Keith Schacht
milestone: Co-founded Lever Works in college and sold it to Leo Media in December 2001 at age 22; co-founded Inventables in 2002 at age 22–23 (materials/innovation platform featured in Forbes/Wired); named among BusinessWeek top 20 entrepreneurs under 25; TED speaker by 2005 (age 25).

name: Bonnie Berger
milestone: Won the Machtey Award (best student paper) at FOCS 1989 at about age 24 for work on parallel algorithms with John Rompel; completed MIT Ph.D. in 1990 (age ~25) under Silvio Micali, then stayed at MIT for postdoc and joined the faculty in 1992.

name: Charlie Cheever
milestone: Joined Facebook in January 2006 at age 24 as an early engineer/manager after Amazon; contributed to News Feed, Facebook Connect, Gaming, and Video, and built internal tool BunnyLol—material early-platform engineering milestone before co-founding Quora at 27.

name: John Cook
milestone: In 1996 (~age 20), co-created and released Team Fortress, a class-based multiplayer Quake mod that became one of the most-played Quake mods worldwide and led to Valve hiring him and Robin Walker in 1998 (~age 22).

name: David J. Brown
milestone: In 1982, at about age 25, co-founded Silicon Graphics (SGI) as one of seven Stanford technical staff who joined Jim Clark to build the company that pioneered 3D graphics workstations.

name: Pavel Durov
milestone: Co-founded and launched VKontakte (VK) for beta in September 2006 at age 21; the network scaled to 1 million users by July 2007 (age 22) and became Russia’s dominant social network.

name: Henrique Dubugras
milestone: Co-founded Brazilian payments company Pagar.me in 2013 at about age 17–18; grew it to ~100–150 employees and ~$1.5B GMV, then sold it to StoneCo in 2016 at age ~21; co-founded Brex in January 2017 at age ~21–22 via Y Combinator.

name: Nishad Singh
milestone: After graduating UC Berkeley EE summa cum laude (2017) and a brief Facebook engineering stint, joined Alameda Research full-time (Dec 2017, age ~22), became Engineering Manager (~June 2018) then Head of Engineering, and by spring 2019 (~age 24) was Director of Engineering at FTX with a large equity stake—all well before age 26.

name: Lachy Groom
milestone: By age ~13–17 sold multiple online businesses (including a PSD-to-WordPress service bought by a U.S. competitor); at ~18 moved to San Francisco and joined Stripe as roughly employee #30 (sources cite ~2012–2014), rising to Head of Issuing—all well before age 26.

name: Aaron Iba
milestone: Co-founded AppJet (YC, 2007) at age ~24; launched Etherpad (first widely noted web realtime collaborative editor, 2008–2009) and sold AppJet/Etherpad to Google in December 2009 at age 26.

name: Ruchi Sanghvi
milestone: In 2005 at age 23 she joined Facebook as its first female engineer; in September 2006 at age 24 she was a primary engineer on the first News Feed launch and authored the launch blog post.

name: Adam Paszke
milestone: In 2016 at about age 20–21, while a University of Warsaw CS/Math student on a FAIR internship under Soumith Chintala, he co-created and shipped the initial PyTorch release (alpha September 2016) as an original author of the framework.

name: Kevin Mitnick
milestone: By age 17 (1980–81), arrested for unauthorized access after social-engineering and breaching Pacific Bell COSMOS systems; already known for phone phreaking and computer intrusion that made him a lasting security-world figure long before his 1995 FBI capture.

name: Adrian Lamo
milestone: In 2001–2002 (ages ~20–21), publicly documented grey-hat intrusions into Yahoo!, Microsoft/Excite@Home, WorldCom, and The New York Times networks—national media coverage and a 2003 federal arrest/2004 felony guilty plea followed while still under 26.

name: Kim Dotcom
milestone: Arrested in 1994 (~20) for trafficking stolen phone calling-card numbers and, in 1998 (~24), convicted in Germany on 11 counts of computer fraud and 10 of data espionage—establishing him as a high-profile European hacker-entrepreneur well before Megaupload.

name: Julian Assange
milestone: In December 1996 (age 25), pleaded guilty to 24 Australian computer-hacking charges stemming from International Subversives intrusions (including Nortel and broader military/industrial targets), receiving a fine and good-behaviour bond after a high-profile federal investigation—material early notoriety years before WikiLeaks.

name: Chelsea Manning
milestone: In early 2010, at age 22, as a U.S. Army intelligence analyst in Iraq, leaked nearly 750,000 classified military and diplomatic documents to WikiLeaks—the largest unauthorized disclosure of U.S. state secrets in history at the time—including the Collateral Murder video, Iraq/Afghan war logs, and diplomatic cables.

name: Joe Lonsdale
milestone: Co-founded Palantir Technologies around 2003–2004 (company incorporated May 2003; prototype work 2004) with Peter Thiel, Alex Karp, Stephen Cohen, and Nathan Gettings while finishing Stanford CS—age ~21—building data analytics software for intelligence and defense.

name: Stephen Cohen
milestone: Co-founded Palantir Technologies in 2003 at age 20 (born September 30, 1982; company founded May 6, 2003) as a Stanford computer science student; credited with building the initial Palantir prototype in about eight weeks and remaining president and board member.

name: Nathan Gettings
milestone: Co-founded Palantir Technologies on May 6, 2003, at age 26 (born March 1977) as a former PayPal engineer; with Thiel funding, built early prototype applying PayPal-style fraud detection techniques to intelligence analysis alongside Stanford students Lonsdale and Cohen.

name: Erik Finman
milestone: Became a self-made bitcoin millionaire by age 18 after investing a $1,000 grandmother gift into bitcoin at age 12 in 2011 (~$12/BTC), then compounding holdings; widely covered as a teenage crypto millionaire while still under 26.

name: Jesse Pollak
milestone: Co-founded Clef (passwordless authentication) around 2012–2013 at about age 22–23; ran the company for roughly five years before joining Coinbase via acquisition path in 2017, establishing early founder/operator track record well before creating Base in his 30s.

name: Alfred Lin
milestone: In 1996, at about age 24, dropped out of a Stanford PhD program to join Tony Hsieh's LinkExchange as CFO; roughly 18 months later (~1997–1998, age ~25–26) LinkExchange sold to Microsoft for $265 million—material early operator/exit milestone by 26.

name: David Baszucki
milestone: In July 1989 at age 26 he co-founded Knowledge Revolution with his brother Greg and shipped Interactive Physics, a 2D educational physics simulator that became widely used in classrooms (company later acquired by MSC Software in 1998 for ~$20M).

name: James W. Hunt
milestone: In 1976 at age 23–24 he co-authored with Douglas McIlroy the Bell Labs technical report 'An Algorithm for Differential File Comparison' (Hunt–McIlroy algorithm), foundational to Unix diff; in 1977 (age 24–25) he published the Hunt–Szymanski LCS algorithm in Communications of the ACM.

name: Pamela Fox
milestone: By 2012 at age ~26 she joined Coursera as an early frontend/full-stack engineer after ~5 years as one of Google's early developer advocates (Maps API community), a material early-career platform role begun ~2007 at age ~21.

name: Alexandra Boltasseva
milestone: Completed a Ph.D. in electrical engineering at the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) in 2004 at age 26, with dissertation work on integrated-optics components using long-range surface plasmon polaritons, and received a Danish Technical Research Council Talent Project grant the same year.

name: Joy Buolamwini
milestone: Named a 2013 Rhodes Scholar in November 2012 at age 22 after graduating Georgia Tech in computer science; by age 26 (2016) she had also founded the Algorithmic Justice League while at MIT Media Lab.

name: Naval Ravikant
milestone: In 1999 at age 24–25 he co-founded Epinions, a consumer product-review site that raised ~$45M in venture capital from Benchmark and August Capital.

name: Liang Rubo
milestone: In 2009 at about age 26 he co-founded the vertical real-estate search portal Jiujiufang (99fang) with college roommate Zhang Yiming—a material startup founding before ByteDance.

name: Emma Brunskill
milestone: Around 2000–2001 (~age 19–20) she won a Rhodes Scholarship after entering the University of Washington at 15 and graduating magna cum laude in computer engineering and physics in 2000; she earned an Oxford neuroscience master's in 2002.

name: William Hockey
milestone: At age 21 (~2010–2012) he cofounded Plaid with Zachary Perret in New York, building bank-linking infrastructure later used by major fintech apps.

name: Darragh Buckley
milestone: In 2010 at about age 25–26 he joined Stripe as its first employee and spent six years as a core early operator/engineer while the company built modern online payments infrastructure.

name: Apoorva Mehta
milestone: Founded Instacart in 2012 at age 26 and entered Y Combinator’s Summer 2012 batch, launching the on-demand grocery marketplace that later became a multi-billion-dollar public company.

name: David S. Miller
milestone: In 1996 at age 21–22, with Miguel de Icaza, ported the Linux kernel to Sun SPARC and presented the work at USENIX; by the late 1990s he was primary maintainer of the Linux IP networking layer while still under 26.

name: Olaf Carlson-Wee
milestone: In 2013 at age ~24, after cold-emailing his Vassar Bitcoin thesis to Coinbase’s founders, he became Coinbase’s first employee, ran early support/risk, and was paid in bitcoin for three years.

name: Gayle Laakmann McDowell
milestone: In 2008 at age ~26 she self-published the first edition of Cracking the Coding Interview and built CareerCup into the defining interview-prep platform for big-tech software hiring.

name: Serge Belongie
milestone: Co-founded DigitalPersona (Digital Persona) around 1996 (age ~22) while an undergraduate at Caltech, helping create what was described as the world's first mass-market fingerprint identification device; principal architect of its fingerprint recognition algorithm.

name: Aubrey Edwards
milestone: Served as producer (lead/credited producer) of Scribblenauts Unlimited, a major commercial Wii U/3DS/PC title released November 2012 when she was 25, after starting as tools programmer on the original Scribblenauts (2009, age 22) and producing Super Scribblenauts.

name: Charles Kuta
milestone: In November 1981 at age ~25 he co-founded Silicon Graphics with James H. Clark and other Stanford colleagues; he contributed to the pipelined Geometry Engine for hardware 3D transforms.

name: Zach Perret
milestone: In late 2012 / early 2013 at age 25 he co-founded Plaid with William Hockey (after Bain 2010–2012), starting the fintech API company that became critical banking infrastructure.

name: Dmitriy Zaporozhets
milestone: Created the open-source GitLab project from Ukraine in October 2011 (with Valery Sizov) as a self-hosted Git collaboration tool while working as a web developer, at about age 24; later co-founded GitLab Inc. with Sid Sijbrandij.

name: Amitt Mahajan
milestone: Co-founded MyMiniLife (2007) and, after Zynga's mid-2009 acquisition, co-created/led engineering for FarmVille (launched June 2009), which rapidly became Facebook's leading social game—while under 30 on Forbes 30 Under 30 (2012) and a 2006 UIUC CS graduate, placing the FarmVille milestone at about age 24–25.

name: Adrian Carmack
milestone: Co-founded id Software on February 1, 1991 at age 21 with John Carmack, John Romero, and Tom Hall after meeting at Softdisk; as lead artist shipped Commander Keen (1990–91), Wolfenstein 3D (1992, age 23), and Doom (December 1993, age 24), defining the studio's gore aesthetic and the term 'gibs'.

name: Luke Farritor
milestone: In October 2023, at age ~21, won the Vesuvius Challenge First Letters Prize ($40,000) as the first person to recover a complete word (ΠΟΡΦΥΡΑϹ, 'purple') from an unopened Herculaneum scroll using machine learning on CT scans.

name: Christopher Olah
milestone: In 2012, at age 19, awarded a $100,000 Thiel Fellowship for independent technical work after dropping out of University of Toronto; by 2015 (~age 22) he was an intern/research scientist track at Google Brain working on neural network visualization.

name: Trip Adler
milestone: In March 2007, at age ~22–23, co-founded and launched Scribd out of a San Francisco apartment after Y Combinator (summer 2006), building one of the early successful document-sharing and later ebook subscription platforms.

name: Brittney Exline
milestone: In May 2011, at age 19, graduated cum laude from the University of Pennsylvania with a BSE in computer science—reported as Penn’s youngest engineer graduate and the nation’s youngest African-American engineer—after entering an Ivy League program at 15.

name: Gary Wang
milestone: In or around October 2017 at about age 24, he left Google Flights and co-founded Alameda Research with Sam Bankman-Fried; in 2019 at about age 26 he co-founded crypto exchange FTX as CTO.

name: Aisha Bowe
milestone: By 2009 at about age 23–24 she completed a University of Michigan aerospace BS (2008) and space systems engineering MS (2009) and joined NASA Ames in the AST Flight and Fluid Mechanics group working on air-traffic management algorithms.

name: Grady Booch
milestone: In 1981 at age 25–26 he became Chief Scientist of Rational Software (Rational Machines) from the company's founding by Paul Levy and Mike Devlin, beginning a multi-decade leadership role in software engineering tools and methods.

name: Brett Adcock
milestone: In early 2012, at age 25, co-founded Vettery (later Hired), an AI-based online talent marketplace with Adam Goldstein out of NYU’s Varick Street Incubator; the company later sold to Adecco for about $100–110M in 2018.

name: Daniel Gross
milestone: In 2010, at about age 18–19, accepted as the then-youngest Y Combinator founder (W10) and co-founded Greplin (later Cue); by ~19 raised Sequoia capital and by 2013 (age ~22) sold Cue to Apple for a reported $40–60M.

name: Alec Muffett
milestone: In 1990–1991, at age 22–23 while a Unix systems programmer at the University of Wales Aberystwyth, created and publicly released Crack (first public Usenet release v2.7a on 15 July 1991)—the first widely used standalone Unix password cracker, later foundational for admin security tooling and CrackLib.

name: Walter Bright
milestone: Around 1977–1978, at about age 18 while a student at Caltech, designed and implemented Empire, an early full-featured computer strategy wargame on the PDP-10 that spread widely (later DECUS distribution) and became a foundational 4X/empire-building computer game lineage.

name: David Stavens
milestone: In 2005, at about age 23, co-created Stanford’s Stanley autonomous vehicle team that won the DARPA Grand Challenge; self-supervised vision/terrain work was central, later recognized with a Stanford AI Lab gold medal and Smithsonian display of Stanley.

name: Safal Bora
milestone: In December 2024 at age 26 he crossed 2500 FIDE and completed FIDE Grandmaster requirements after earning his final GM norm in July 2024.

name: Su Zhu
milestone: In 2012 at about age 24–25 he co-founded Three Arrows Capital (3AC) in San Francisco with Kyle Davies, raising ~$1M seed by borrowing from their parents.

name: Sebastien Pahl
milestone: Around 2008–2010 (while finishing EPITECH, ~age 22–24) he co-founded dotCloud with Solomon Hykes and Kamel Founadi; the company entered Y Combinator Summer 2010 and later became Docker Inc.

name: Divya Gokulnath
milestone: In 2011 at age 24 she co-founded Byju's in Bangalore with Byju Raveendran after several years teaching in his test-prep classes.

name: TJ Holowaychuk
milestone: In 2010 at about age 23 he created Express.js (initial versions early 2010; v1 later that year), which became the dominant Node.js web framework.

name: Karina Nguyen
milestone: By about age 23–24 (Claude 3 era, 2023–2024) she led post-training and evaluation work on Anthropic's Claude 3 models; earlier twenties also included design/engineering at Square, Dropbox, and the New York Times.

name: Jon Bentley
milestone: In 1975 at age 22 he published the seminal k-d tree paper 'Multidimensional binary search trees used for associative searching' (CACM), developed around his Stanford B.S. work; PhD UNC Chapel Hill followed in 1976 at age 23.

name: Nick Frosst
milestone: In 2019 at age 26 he co-founded Cohere with Aidan Gomez and Ivan Zhang after serving as an early Geoffrey Hinton hire at Google Brain Toronto (from 2016, age 23).

name: Bing Xu
milestone: In 2014, at about age 23 (BEng BUPT 2009–2013; MSc Alberta beginning 2013), co-authored the seminal NeurIPS paper Generative Adversarial Nets with Goodfellow, Bengio, and others—one of the most cited papers in modern AI—and in 2015 co-created the MXNet deep-learning framework.

name: Angela Benton
milestone: In August 2007, at age 26, launched Black Web 2.0, the leading online publication covering Black innovators and digital strategy in technology, which established her as a go-to voice and platform-builder for underrepresented founders.

name: Tim Berners-Lee
milestone: While a contractor at CERN in 1980 (age 25), proposed a hypertext information-sharing system and built the ENQUIRE prototype, the direct conceptual precursor to the World Wide Web.

name: Trevor Blackwell
milestone: Joined Viaweb in September 1995 at age 25 during his Harvard CS PhD and wrote core image-rendering, order-processing, and statistics software for the pioneering web-based online store platform later acquired by Yahoo.

name: Marco Arment
milestone: In 2006–2007, at age 24, co-built Tumblr with David Karp and became its founding lead developer and CTO from launch, helping create one of the defining Web 2.0 microblogging platforms.

name: Nikolai Durov
milestone: In October 2006, at age 25, co-founded VKontakte (VK) with brother Pavel and served as lead developer/CTO of Russia's dominant social network, after already winning three IMO gold medals (1996–98) and two ACM ICPC world titles (2000–01).

name: Tony Fadell
milestone: In 1995, at age 25–26, was hired by Philips, co-founded its Mobile Computing Group, and became CTO/director of engineering, shipping Windows CE handhelds (Velo/Nino) after three years as a systems architect at Apple spinoff General Magic (from 1992, age 23).

name: Vicent Marti
milestone: In 2010 (age ~20), completed a GitHub-sponsored Google Summer of Code project to advance libgit2; by March 2011 GitHub hired him full-time as a GitHubber to maintain libgit2—the C library later powering core github.com Git operations—after open-source work that eliminated a technical interview.

name: Phil Libin
milestone: In 1997, co-founded Boston software company Engine Five (Engine 5) as CEO with college friends, building online-store software for clients such as Nokia; the company was sold to Vignette in 2000 for about $26 million.

name: Eric Ries
milestone: In April 2004, co-founded IMVU Inc. with Will Harvey (and others) as co-founder and CTO, building a 3D avatar social network that later raised venture funding and became a multi-year growth company.

name: Nick Swinmurn
milestone: Founded Zappos (initially Shoesite.com) in 1999 at about age 26, creating what became a leading online shoe retailer later acquired by Amazon.

name: Jason Citron
milestone: Founded OpenFeint in 2009 (age ~24-25), building a major mobile social gaming network that sold to GREE in 2011 for ~$104M when he was 26.

name: Stanislav Vishnevskiy
milestone: Founded Guildwork (Guild Work) around 2009 at about age 22, building MMO guild management tools that established him as a gaming infrastructure engineer before co-founding Discord.

name: Anthony Levandowski
milestone: Led Berkeley Blue Team’s autonomous motorcycle Ghostrider into the 2004 DARPA Grand Challenge at age 24 (also competed 2005), after earlier student companies including La Raison as a teen/freshman.

name: Luis von Ahn
milestone: Co-created CAPTCHA with Manuel Blum and collaborators around 2000 (published early 2000s) at about age 21-22 while a young CMU researcher, inventing a widely deployed human-vs-bot verification method.

name: Severin Hacker
milestone: Began co-creating Duolingo with advisor Luis von Ahn around 2009 at about age 24-25 during his CMU PhD, founding the company that became the world’s largest language-learning app (company formalization often dated 2011).

name: Daniel Weinand
milestone: Joined Tobias Lütke and Scott Lake in 2005 (~age 26) to co-found the Shopify platform that publicly launched in 2006, after their Snowdevil online store work.

name: Tracy Young
milestone: Co-founded PlanGrid in 2011 at about age 26, building a mobile construction blueprint platform later acquired by Autodesk for ~$875M.

name: Gustaf Alströmer
milestone: Co-founded Heysan (YC W07) around 2007 at about age 24, entering the Y Combinator ecosystem as a founder before later growth leadership at Airbnb and YC partnership.

name: Immad Akhund
milestone: Founded his first startup around 2006 and went through Y Combinator with Clickpass in the mid/late 2000s at about ages 23–24, beginning a multi-startup founder path before Heyzap and Mercury.

name: Deepinder Goyal
milestone: Co-founded Foodiebay (later Zomato) on July 10, 2008 at age 25 while at Bain, launching India's major restaurant discovery and later food-delivery platform.

name: Peyush Bansal
milestone: Incorporated Valyoo Technologies (later Lenskart) in 2008 at age 23 after earlier SearchMyCampus (2007); launched Lenskart online eyewear operations by 2010 at age 25.

name: Jennifer Fleiss
milestone: Co-founded Rent the Runway with Jennifer Hyman in 2008 at about age 25 while at Harvard Business School; site launched November 2009 near age 26.

name: Leila Janah
milestone: Founded Samasource in 2008 at about age 25–26, building a impact-outsourcing company employing people in poverty for digital microwork.

name: Jessica Alba
milestone: Became a globally visible lead actress with Fox's Dark Angel (2000–2002) starting at age 19, after earlier child/teen roles including Camp Nowhere and Idle Hands; major film career by mid-20s (Fantastic Four 2005).

name: Sean Rad
milestone: Co-founded Tinder (launched on college campuses in 2012) at about age 26 inside IAC/Hatch Labs, creating the swipe-based dating product that defined mobile dating.

name: Justin Mateen
milestone: Co-founded Tinder in 2012 at about age 26, serving as CMO and early growth leader of the swipe dating app incubated at Hatch Labs/IAC.

name: José Valim
milestone: Co-founded Plataformatec (~2009–2010) around age 24–25 and joined the Rails Core Team by early 2010 at about age 25; major open-source authority before creating Elixir (~2011–2012).

name: Wang Xing
milestone: Co-founded Xiaonei (campus social network later Renren) in 2005 at age 26, China's early Facebook-like product; sold in 2006 before Fanfou and later Meituan.

name: Richard Liu (Liu Qiangdong)
milestone: Founded Jingdong Multimedia (JD predecessor) in June 1998 at age 25 with ~12,000 yuan savings, opening an electronics booth in Beijing's Zhongguancun.

name: Ilkka Paananen
milestone: Became CEO (and is widely described as co-founder) of mobile game studio Sumea around 2000 at about age 22; studio sold to Digital Chocolate in 2004 while he was ~26.

name: Yu Suzuki
milestone: Designed and released Champion Boxing for Sega's SG-1000 in 1984 at age 26, his first major commercial game credit before Hang-On (1985) and later Virtua Fighter/Shenmue fame.

name: Will Wright
milestone: Designed and published Raid on Bungeling Bay (1984) at age 24, then developed the systems that became SimCity (released 1989) after founding Maxis with Jeff Braun in 1987 (age 27—SimCity launch is post-26 but Bungeling Bay is the ≤26 commercial milestone).

name: American McGee
milestone: Joined id Software in the early 1990s (~age 21) and contributed to Doom/Quake-era titles as level designer/programmer before age 26; major commercial franchise work at the industry's technical frontier.

name: Clifford 'CliffyB' Bleszinski
milestone: Designed Jazz Jackrabbit (1994) at about age 19 as an early Epic MegaGames hit, establishing him as a commercial game designer well before Gears of War.

name: Kim Swift
milestone: Led design of Portal (2007) at Valve at about age 24 after DigiPen student project Narbacular Drop was hired into Valve—defining puzzle-game landmark.

name: Jenova Chen
milestone: Co-founded thatgamecompany in 2006 at about age 25 and released Flow (based on his USC MFA thesis) as a major indie/PSN success defining emotion-focused games.

name: Kellee Santiago
milestone: Produced Cloud (2005) as USC student work and co-founded thatgamecompany in 2006 near age 26–27; Cloud at age ~26 is the dated creative milestone, with company founding straddling the boundary.

name: Richard Garriott
milestone: Commercially published Akalabeth (1980) at about age 18–19 and Ultima I (1981) at ~20, then co-founded Origin Systems in 1983 at age 21–22 to publish Ultima III.

name: Toby Fox
milestone: Released Undertale on September 15, 2015 at age 23, a solo-developed RPG that became a global indie breakout with critical acclaim and massive cultural impact.

name: Edmund McMillen
milestone: Released Gish (2004) at about age 24, which won Indie Game of the Year / Adventure Game of the Year honors and established him as a leading independent designer before Super Meat Boy and The Binding of Isaac.

name: Phil Fish
milestone: Quit studio work and opened Polytron Corporation as a startup in early 2008 (~age 23) after Fez was nominated for IGF awards; Fez had been announced in 2007 and won IGF Excellence in Visual Art in 2008.

name: MacKenzie Scott
milestone: In 1994 at age 24, helped found Amazon with then-husband Jeff Bezos—working on name/business plan, bookkeeping, shipping, and the company's first freight contract as an early key contributor from the garage startup phase.

name: Curtis Priem
milestone: While a staff engineer at Vermont Microsystems (1982–1984), architected IBM's Professional Graphics Adapter—the PC industry's first professional graphics processor—at about age 23–25, a foundational product milestone before later cofounding NVIDIA (1993, age ~34).

name: Jony Ive
milestone: After graduating (1989), cofounded London design consultancy Tangerine around age 22 and by September 1992 (age 25) joined Apple full-time as a product designer—material design-career founding and placement by 26, before later iMac/iPod/iPhone fame.

name: Harley Finkelstein
milestone: Founded a university T-shirt / apparel business at age 17 while at McGill (~2000–2001), scaling nationally—a dated entrepreneurial founding well before joining Shopify in 2010 (~age 26–27) and later becoming President.

name: Anthony Pompliano
milestone: Founded Digaforce (social media analytics) around 2013 at about age 25 and sold it the same year; also founded/exited early startups after Army service before Facebook PM role (~2014–15, age ~26).

name: Brewster Kahle
milestone: Helped start Thinking Machines Corporation around 1983 at about age 22–23 after MIT, serving as lead engineer on parallel supercomputing—material early founding/engineering leadership well before WAIS Inc. (1989) and Internet Archive (1996).

name: Brendan Iribe
milestone: Cofounded Scaleform in 2003 at about age 23–24 with Michael Antonov, building the leading game UI middleware company later sold to Autodesk (2011); Oculus CEO role came later (2012+).

name: Michael Antonov
milestone: Cofounded Scaleform around 2003 during/after college (~age 23) as CTO, building widely embedded game UI middleware later sold to Autodesk; later Oculus chief software architect.

name: Nate Mitchell
milestone: Cofounded Oculus VR in 2012 at about age 24–25 (Dickinson College class of 2009) and helped lead product as the company Kickstarted the Rift and scaled toward Facebook acquisition (2014, age ~27).

name: Harry Stebbings
milestone: Launched The Twenty Minute VC podcast on 10 January 2015 at age 18, interviewing Guy Kawasaki as the first guest and building a distribution platform that made him one of Europe's best-known young VCs.

name: Akshay Kothari
milestone: Co-founded Pulse, a mobile news aggregation app, at Stanford in May 2010 (launched App Store 12 May 2010) at about age 24; app was demoed by Steve Jobs and later sold to LinkedIn for ~$90M.

name: Simon Last
milestone: Co-founded Notion with Ivan Zhao around 2013 at about age 23, serving as technical co-founder/CTO on the all-in-one workspace product that later became a multi-billion-dollar company.

name: Josh Kopelman
milestone: Co-founded Infonautics in 1992 as a Wharton sophomore at about age 20; company IPO'd on Nasdaq in 1996 when he was still in his mid-twenties.

name: Jessica Mah
milestone: Co-founded inDinero in 2009 at age 19 with Berkeley classmate Andy Su, building financial/accounting software for startups; entered Y Combinator and scaled the company through her early twenties.

name: Andy Su
milestone: Co-founded inDinero in 2009 with Jessica Mah as Berkeley CS classmates at about age 19–20, serving as technical co-founder/CTO of the accounting/finance platform.

name: Dennis Crowley
milestone: Created Dodgeball, a pioneering location-based mobile social service, around 2000–2003 (NYU ITP era) at about age 24–26; sold to Google in 2005 when he was ~28–29.

name: Blake Mycoskie
milestone: Founded EZ Laundry while at SMU as a sophomore (~1996-97), scaled it to ~$1M sales with 40+ employees across three universities, and sold his share to his partner in 1999 at about age 22-23; later founded Mycoskie Media sold to Clear Channel.

name: Tim Paterson
milestone: Created QDOS (Quick and Dirty Operating System, later 86-DOS) starting April 1980 at Seattle Computer Products at age 23-24; he has stated he was 24 when he wrote DOS. Microsoft licensed then bought it as the basis of MS-DOS.

name: François Chollet
milestone: Created and released Keras, a widely adopted high-level deep learning library for Python, around February–March 2015 at age 25; joined Google shortly after.

name: Addy Osmani
milestone: At age 16 (2002–2003), built XWebs, an ambitious C++ web browser with multi-connection download optimizations; entered Esat BT Young Scientist of the Year and received Wired and Irish Examiner coverage in January 2003.

name: Theo Browne
milestone: Co-founded Ping Labs (YC W22, Winter 2022) and popularized the T3 Stack / create-t3-app ecosystem around ages 24–25 after Twitch engineering and a fast-growing YouTube channel.

name: Simon Willison
milestone: Co-created the Django web framework while on industrial placement at the Lawrence Journal-World (2003–2004) and saw it open-sourced publicly in July 2005 at age 24.

name: Rich Harris
milestone: Created Ractive.js in 2013 (predecessor to Svelte) while building interactive journalism tooling, at about age 26 under the ~1987 cohort birth year; Svelte v1 followed in 2016.

name: Taylor Otwell
milestone: Created and released Laravel in 2011 as a side project (~age 25) after IT degree work and dissatisfaction with CodeIgniter; framework became the dominant modern PHP stack.

name: Fabien Potencier
milestone: Co-founded Sensio (later SensioLabs) in Paris in 1998 right after studies (~age 19) and founded the Symfony project in 2004 (~age 25), open-sourcing a major PHP framework.

name: Andrew Kelley
milestone: Started designing and announcing the Zig programming language in 2015 at about age 25 as a systems language alternative to C with explicit control-flow and allocation principles.

name: Salvatore Sanfilippo
milestone: Created and released hping, a widely used TCP/IP packet generator/analyzer for network security testing, around 1998 at about age 21 (born 7 March 1977); also invented the idle scan technique implemented by nmap.

name: Hadley Wickham
milestone: Awarded the John Chambers Award for Statistical Computing in 2006 at age 26 for tools for data reshaping and visualisation (early reshape/ggplot ecosystem work during PhD training).

name: Wes McKinney
milestone: Open-sourced pandas in 2009 at about age 24 while working in quant finance at AQR Capital Management after graduating MIT in 2007.

name: Mattt Thompson
milestone: Co-created and open-sourced AFNetworking (first release 2011), which became the dominant iOS/macOS networking library for years, while at Gowalla.

name: Armin Ronacher
milestone: Released Flask (1 April 2010) at age 20 after an April Fools microframework joke; it became one of Python's two dominant web frameworks alongside Django.

name: Kenneth Reitz
milestone: Created Requests ('HTTP for Humans'); first public release 14 February 2011 after writing the initial version at age 21—became Python's default human-friendly HTTP client with tens of millions of daily installs.

name: Brett Cannon
milestone: Received CPython commit rights on 18 April 2003 (age ~24 per batch birth year 1979), beginning a 20+ year core-developer career including importlib and packaging leadership.

name: Jessie Frazelle
milestone: Joined Docker Inc as software engineer/core maintainer (Nov 2014–Mar 2016), becoming one of the most visible core maintainers of the dominant container runtime during Docker's peak growth (age ~25; self-stated age 27 in Aug 2016).

name: Chris Coyier
milestone: Launched CSS-Tricks in June 2007 at age 26 (born August 1980), building the defining CSS education blog of the era.

name: Max Stoiber
milestone: Co-created styled-components with Glen Maddern in October 2016 (~age 22), a CSS-in-JS library that became a default React styling approach with massive adoption.

name: Sebastian McKenzie
milestone: Created 6to5 (later Babel) in September 2014 at age 17 while still in Australian high school; the project became the dominant ES6+ JavaScript compiler ecosystem tool.

name: Henry Zhu
milestone: Became primary community maintainer of Babel after Sebastian McKenzie stepped back (~2016–2017, ~age 23–24), then went full-time on Babel via community funding—sustaining a critical JS infrastructure project.

name: Christopher Chedeau
milestone: Co-created React Native on Facebook's original team (public 2015, ~age 25), helping define cross-platform React mobile development; earlier popularized CSS-in-JS ideas.

name: Andrew Clark
milestone: Co-created Redux with Dan Abramov in 2015 (~age 26), establishing the dominant React application state architecture of the mid-2010s.

name: Sophie Alpert
milestone: Became React's top external committer shortly after open-source release (2013–2014, ~age 21–22) and joined Facebook's React team in 2015 (~age 23), later leading the team through adolescent years of the library.

name: Shu Ding
milestone: Created SWR with Guillermo Rauch in 2019 (~age 25), the first major hook-based stale-while-revalidate data-fetching library; also joined Vercel early (2018) and designed the Next.js website.

name: Tim Neutkens
milestone: Became co-author of Next.js around age 20 after major open-source contributions, then joined ZEIT/Vercel end of 2017 as the sole full-time Next.js maintainer.

name: Varun Mohan
milestone: Co-founded Codeium (later Windsurf) in 2021 at about age 25 with MIT classmate Douglas Chen, building an AI coding assistant that scaled to mass developer adoption and unicorn outcomes.

name: Jim Fan
milestone: Became OpenAI's first research intern in 2016 (~age 22) after graduating Columbia CS as class valedictorian (Illig Medal), then started a Stanford PhD with Fei-Fei Li—material early research-career milestone.

name: Courtland Allen
milestone: In fall 2010 founded Taskforce (email-to-tasks product) and was accepted to Y Combinator Winter 2011 at age 23–24—an independently documented funded-founder milestone before age 26.

name: Jason Wei
milestone: Lead author of chain-of-thought prompting (arXiv Jan 2022) and earlier FLAN instruction-tuning paper (arXiv Sept 2021) while at Google Brain—field-defining LLM reasoning work at age ~23–24 (Dartmouth CS ’20; Fairfax County / TJHSST pipeline consistent with ~1998 birth).

name: Barret Zoph
milestone: First author with Quoc V. Le on Neural Architecture Search with Reinforcement Learning (arXiv Nov 2016; ICLR 2017)—foundational AutoML/NAS paper produced during Google Brain Residency, at age ~26 under CSV/queue birth year 1990.

name: Patrick Campbell
milestone: In 2012 at age 24, founded Price Intelligently (later ProfitWell), a SaaS pricing/retention platform he bootstrapped and later sold to Paddle for ~$200M.

name: Fabrice Bellard
milestone: At age 17 (1989–1990), created and released LZEXE, a widely used DOS executable compressor—an early, independently verified technical milestone before FFmpeg/QEMU fame.

name: Ben Awad
milestone: By Nov 2021 at age 24, had built a large independent developer audience (~360k YouTube; nearly 700k TikTok) while shipping open-source products (e.g. DogeHouse, VSinder), establishing a material builder-creator platform before 26.

name: Kyle Cook
milestone: Built Web Dev Simplified into a major free web-dev education brand after launching May 2018 (~age 23), reaching roughly 500k YouTube subscribers by ~April 2021 (~age 26).

name: Window Snyder
milestone: Joined elite consultancy @stake as roughly the 10th employee in the late 1990s / ~2000 (~age 24–25) and rose in security architecture before leaving in 2002 (~age 27), establishing herself among the first generation of specialist application-security leaders.

name: Alex Stamos
milestone: Co-founded iSEC Partners in 2004 at about age 25 with four colleagues, building an elite security consultancy later acquired by NCC Group.

name: Peiter Zatko
milestone: Published the influential 'How to Write Buffer Overflows' paper (Oct 20, 1995) at age 24 and authored early L0pht security tools/advisories (including L0phtCrack lineage) that shaped full-disclosure exploit research.

name: Tsutomu Shimomura
milestone: Became a research scientist in computational physics at UC San Diego and senior fellow at the San Diego Supercomputer Center in 1989 (~age 25) after Caltech study under Richard Feynman and staff physicist work at Los Alamos.

name: Limor Fried
milestone: Founded Adafruit Industries in 2005 (~age 25 under CSV/timeline ~1980) from MIT after SB (2003) and MEng (2005), launching a defining open-source electronics kit company for hobbyists.

name: Bunnie Huang
milestone: As an MIT EE PhD student, reverse-engineered the original Microsoft Xbox security system after its Nov 2001 launch and published the foundational AI Memo 'Keeping Secrets in Hardware: the Microsoft Xbox Case Study' (May 2002), the first widely cited public analysis of Xbox hardware security, at about age 26–27.

name: Naomi Wu
milestone: Designed and publicly documented the 3D-printed Wu Ying 'hacker heels' with embedded pentest tools (keylogger, wireless router, lockpicks) in 2015 at about age 21, launching her SexyCyborg persona as a widely covered Shenzhen maker; by 2018 (age 23–24) she was the first Chinese person on the cover of Make magazine.

name: Ankit Bhati
milestone: Co-founded Ola Cabs (ANI Technologies) with Bhavish Aggarwal in December 2010 / early 2011 at about age 23, serving as technical cofounder/CTO of what became one of India's largest ride-hailing platforms.

name: Tanay Kothari
milestone: Co-founded Wispr (later Wispr Flow) around 2021 at age ~23 after prior teen products (including Convert.cc with millions of users) and selling FeatherX, an e-commerce personalization startup built around Stanford graduation; Forbes 30 Under 30 (Consumer Technology) in Dec 2022 at age 24.

name: Aditya Grover
milestone: Published node2vec (KDD 2016 with Jure Leskovec), a foundational network representation-learning paper with 16k+ citations, at about age 22 while a Stanford PhD student shortly after IIT Delhi undergrad (2015).

name: Antirez
milestone: In 1998 at age 21, invented and published the idle scan (blind TCP port scan) and released hping—security tools later adopted into Nmap and industry practice—years before creating Redis.

name: Web Dev Simplified
milestone: Channel brand of Kyle Cook: launched May 2018 and scaled to ~500k YouTube subscribers by ~April 2021 (~age 26 for Cook, b. 1995).

name: Mudge
milestone: Published the influential 'How to Write Buffer Overflows' paper (Oct 20, 1995) at age 24 and authored early L0pht security tools/advisories (including L0phtCrack lineage) that shaped full-disclosure exploit research.

name: Patrick McKenzie
milestone: Launched Bingo Card Creator in 2006 at about age 22—an early successful single-founder desktop/SaaS product for teachers that later funded full-time entrepreneurship and the influential patio11 blog/HN persona.

name: Dan Shipper
milestone: Co-founded Fire and Ice (//FIRE//) around 2009–2010 at about age 19–20, an early social/discovery product that drew TechCrunch attention and led to Harvard Business Review recognition as a young entrepreneur by age ~20.

name: Nathan Baschez
milestone: Co-founded Product Hunt with Ryan Hoover in November 2013 at about age 25, building one of the defining early distribution platforms for startups and makers.

name: Linus Sebastian
milestone: Created the Linus Tech Tips YouTube channel on November 24, 2008 at age 22 while producing tech content for NCIX, establishing the brand that later became Linus Media Group and one of the largest tech YouTube networks.

name: iJustine
milestone: Launched the iJustine YouTube channel with first videos on May 12, 2006 at age 22, then broke out in 2007 (age 23) with a viral video documenting a 300-page iPhone bill that brought millions of views and mainstream tech-creator fame.

name: Lewis Hilsenteger
milestone: Co-founded Unbox Therapy with Jack McCann in December 2010 at age 25, building a defining consumer-tech unboxing and review channel from a Toronto-area base.

name: Felix Kjellberg
milestone: Registered the PewDiePie YouTube channel on April 29, 2010 at age 20 and rapidly became the defining Let's Play / comedy-gaming creator of the early 2010s, reaching industry-leading subscriber counts well before age 26.

name: Tyler Blevins
milestone: Began playing Halo 3 professionally in 2009 at about age 18 (MLG circuit), establishing a multi-year esports career with teams including Cloud9 and Team Liquid well before the Fortnite streaming explosion.

name: N0tail
milestone: Joined Fnatic's European Dota 2 roster on March 30, 2012 at age 18 after HoN success, becoming a top-tier professional player; later co-founded OG and won The International twice (2018–19), still within/near the age-26 window for TI8.

name: Jared Isaacman
milestone: Founded United Bank Card (later Harbortouch / Shift4 Payments) in 1999 at age 16 after leaving high school, building a point-of-sale payments company he has led as CEO since inception.

name: Chris Messina
milestone: Proposed the Twitter hashtag in a public tweet on August 23, 2007 at age 26 (#barcamp), creating the social-media convention later adopted globally for topic grouping.

name: Tantek Çelik
milestone: Joined Microsoft in March 1997 at about age 22 and became a principal engineer on Internet Explorer/CSS (including Mac IE / Tasman-related web standards work), establishing a career-defining systems role in browser CSS implementation well before age 26.

name: Ryan Block
milestone: Joined Engadget as a part-time reporter in June 2004 (~age 21–22), went full-time June 2005, and by September 2005 was publicly identified as managing editor of Engadget at age 23; became editor-in-chief in 2007 (~age 24–25), leading one of the era's top consumer-tech blogs before AOL ownership.

name: Elizabeth Spiers
milestone: As founding editor, launched Gawker.com with Nick Denton in December 2002 at age 25 (born Dec 11, 1976), defining the voice of the flagship Gawker Media gossip blog and helping invent a durable model of snarky, high-velocity media blogging.

name: Rand Fishkin
milestone: Co-founded SEOMoz (later Moz) with his mother Gillian Muessig in 2004 at about age 25, after launching the SEOmoz blog in late 2003; the firm became a leading SEO consulting community and later a major SEO SaaS platform.

name: Dwarkesh Patel
milestone: Built Dwarkesh Podcast (started 2020 as The Lunar Society while a UT Austin CS student, age 19–20) into a leading AI/tech interview platform; named to TIME100 AI 2024 at age 23–24 for deeply researched conversations with figures such as Ilya Sutskever, Andrej Karpathy, and Mark Zuckerberg.

name: Ninja
milestone: Reached 500,000 Twitch followers by September 2017 at age 26, won the PUBG Gamescom Invitational Squads in August 2017, and in March 2018 at age 26 played Fortnite with Drake breaking the Twitch concurrent viewer record with 630,000 viewers, becoming the most-followed streamer on the platform.

name: N0tail (Johan Sundstein)
milestone: Won The International 2018 and 2019 back-to-back with OG, becoming the highest-earning esports player in history (~$7.1M+ in prize money) by age 26; also won four Dota Major championships and multiple DreamHack titles in Heroes of Newerth before transitioning to Dota 2.

name: Robert Morris
milestone: Released the Morris worm from MIT on November 2, 1988 while a Cornell first-year graduate student at age 22—the first widely disruptive internet worm—and became the first person convicted under the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act.

name: Unbox Therapy
milestone: Lewis Hilsenteger co-created the Unbox Therapy YouTube channel in December 2010 at about age 25, founding one of the definitive tech unboxing brands (later tens of millions of subscribers).

name: PewDiePie
milestone: Became the most-subscribed channel on YouTube on August 15, 2013 at age 23, and was the most-viewed channel from December 2014 to February 2017.

name: Alexander Wang
milestone: Launched his eponymous fashion label in 2005 at age 21 and presented his first full women's ready-to-wear runway collection at New York Fashion Week in Fall 2007 at age 23; won the CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund in 2008 at age 24.

name: Olivier Rousteing
milestone: Appointed creative director of Balmain in April 2011 at age 25, becoming the youngest non-founding designer to lead a major Paris house since Yves Saint Laurent and the first Black person to lead a heritage French house.

name: Simone Rocha
milestone: Debuted her graduate collection at London Fashion Week and the Tate Modern in September 2010 at age 24, launching her eponymous label with immediate stocking at Dover Street Market and Colette.

name: Jonathan Anderson
milestone: Launched the JW Anderson menswear label in 2008 at age 23 and presented his first catwalk collection at London Fashion Week in 2010 at age 25, receiving British Fashion Council NewGen sponsorship.

name: Christopher Kane
milestone: Launched his eponymous label in 2006 at age 24 with a debut show at London Fashion Week that was lauded by international critics, and was immediately hired by Versace to work on their Atelier couture collection.

name: Molly Goddard
milestone: Showed her first collection off-schedule at London Fashion Week in September 2014 at age 25, with Dover Street Market and IT Hong Kong placing orders the next day, launching her eponymous label.

name: Grace Wales Bonner
milestone: Founded the Wales Bonner label in 2014 at age 24 after graduating from Central Saint Martins, debuted the 'Ebonics' collection at Fashion East in London in 2015, and won the LVMH Young Designer Prize in 2016 at age 25-26.

name: Tyler Mitchell
milestone: Shot the cover of American Vogue's September 2018 issue featuring Beyonce at age 23, becoming the first African American photographer to shoot a Vogue cover; Smithsonian National Portrait Gallery acquired one of the portraits in 2019.

name: Nadine Ijewere
milestone: Became the first woman of colour to shoot a cover for any Vogue edition worldwide with her January 2019 British Vogue cover featuring Dua Lipa, Binx Walton, and Letitia Wright at age 26.

name: Petra Collins
milestone: Opened her first solo exhibition 'Discharge' at Capricious 88 Gallery in New York in February 2014 at age 21, cementing her position as a leading voice in feminist photography and the 'female gaze' movement.

name: Jadé Fadojutimi
milestone: Had her first solo exhibition 'Heliophobia' at Pippy Houldsworth Gallery in London in December 2017 at age 24, with immediate representation and acquisitions by Tate, ICA Miami, and Dallas Museum of Art following.

name: FEWOCiOUS (Victor Langlois)
milestone: Sold his NFT artwork 'Hello, i'm Victor (FEWOCiOUS) and This Is My Life' at Christie's in June 2021 for $2.16 million at age 18, becoming the youngest artist to have a solo sale at Christie's.

name: Diana Sinclair
milestone: Headlined the inaugural sale on Christie's 3.0 NFT platform in September 2022 at age 18 with a solo exhibition 'Phases' at Christie's New York galleries, and previously collaborated with the Whitney Houston estate on an NFT that sold for $1 million in November 2021 at age 17.

name: Richard Quinn
milestone: Won the H&M Design Award 2017 in November 2016 at age 26, receiving €50,000 and a year-long mentorship, and established his eponymous label in 2016 after graduating from the Central Saint Martins MA course.

name: Campbell Addy
milestone: Held his debut solo exhibition 'Matthew 7:7 & 8' at KK Outlet in London in 2017 at age 24, and founded Nii Journal and Nii Agency in 2016 while still at Central Saint Martins, establishing himself as a photographer and publisher.

name: Amit Elor
milestone: Won Olympic gold medal in women's freestyle wrestling 68kg at the 2024 Paris Olympics at age 20, becoming the youngest US wrestler ever to win Olympic gold.

name: Summer McIntosh
milestone: Won three Olympic gold medals (200m butterfly, 200m IM, 400m IM) and one silver (400m freestyle) at the Paris 2024 Olympics at age 17, becoming the first Canadian athlete to win three golds at a single Olympic Games. Also holds world records in the 200m butterfly, 200m IM, 400m IM, and 400m freestyle.

name: Lando Norris
milestone: Achieved his first Formula One podium finish at age 20 at the 2020 Austrian Grand Prix, becoming one of the youngest podium finishers in F1 history.

name: Oscar Piastri
milestone: Achieved his first Formula 1 podium at the 2023 Japanese Grand Prix at age 22, and won his first Grand Prix at the 2024 Hungarian GP at age 23.

name: Victor Wembanyama
milestone: Selected #1 overall in the 2023 NBA Draft and named an NBA All-Star in 2025 at age 21, after being the unanimous Rookie of the Year. Won Defensive Player of the Year and reached the NBA Finals in 2026.

name: Alphonso Davies
milestone: Won the UEFA Champions League with Bayern Munich in August 2020 at age 19, becoming the first Canadian men's player to win the competition. Named Bundesliga Rookie of the Season the same year.

name: Gabriela Fundora
milestone: Became the youngest undisputed boxing world champion across all divisions and genders in the four-belt era at age 22 in November 2024, unifying the WBA, WBC, IBF, WBO, and The Ring flyweight titles.

name: Alina Zagitova
milestone: Won the 2018 Olympic gold medal in women's singles figure skating at age 15, becoming the second-youngest Olympic champion in women's singles behind Tara Lipinski. Also won the 2019 World Championships.

name: David Popovici
milestone: Won the 100m and 200m freestyle at the 2022 World Aquatics Championships at age 17, becoming the first male swimmer in 49 years to sweep both events. Won Olympic gold in the 200m freestyle at Paris 2024 at age 19.

name: Anathan 'ana' Pham
milestone: Won The International 2018 (Dota 2's world championship) at age 18 with team OG, and repeated as champion at The International 2019. Also won two Dota Major championships.

name: Danil 'donk' Kryshkovets
milestone: Won the Perfect World Shanghai Major 2024 at age 17, becoming the youngest-ever Major champion in Counter-Strike history. Named HLTV Player of the Year 2024 at 17 years and 352 days old.

name: Kaylia Nemour
milestone: Won Olympic gold on uneven bars at the 2024 Paris Olympics at age 17, becoming the first gymnast from any African nation to win an Olympic medal. Also won silver at the 2023 World Championships.

name: Arisa Trew
milestone: Won the gold medal in women's park skateboarding at the 2024 Paris Olympics at age 14, becoming Australia's youngest ever Olympic champion. First woman to land a 720 and 900 in competition.

name: Léon Marchand
milestone: Won four individual Olympic gold medals at the 2024 Paris Olympics at age 22, becoming the fourth swimmer in Olympic history to win four individual golds at a single Games and France's biggest star of the Games.

name: Momiji Nishiya
milestone: Won the first-ever Olympic gold medal in women's street skateboarding at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics at age 13, becoming the youngest Japanese Olympic gold medalist in history.

name: Cocona Hiraki
milestone: Won silver medal in women's park skateboarding at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics at age 12, becoming the youngest Japanese Summer Olympic athlete ever, and won a second silver at the Paris 2024 Olympics at age 15.

name: Rayssa Leal
milestone: Won silver medal in women's street skateboarding at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics at age 13, becoming Brazil's youngest-ever Olympic medalist, and won bronze at the Paris 2024 Olympics at age 16.

name: Sky Brown
milestone: Won bronze medal in women's park skateboarding at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics at age 13, becoming Great Britain's youngest-ever Olympic medallist, and won a second bronze at Paris 2024. Also won the 2023 and 2025 World Skateboarding Championship gold medals.

name: Quan Hongchan
milestone: Won Olympic gold medal in the 10-meter platform diving at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics at age 14, and won two more gold medals (individual and synchronized 10m platform) at the Paris 2024 Olympics at age 17.

name: Kimi Antonelli
milestone: Debuted in Formula 1 for Mercedes at the 2025 Australian Grand Prix at age 18, becoming the third-youngest F1 driver ever. Won 6 Grands Prix by mid-2026, became the youngest-ever F1 polesitter, and led the World Drivers' Championship at age 19.

name: Tomokazu Harimoto
milestone: Became the youngest-ever ITTF World Tour men's singles winner at 14 years and 61 days (2017 Czech Open), the youngest Japanese national table tennis singles champion at 14 (January 2018), and the youngest ITTF World Tour Grand Finals champion at 15 (December 2018). Reached world #2 ranking by November 2022.

name: Félix Lebrun
milestone: Won two bronze medals (individual and team) at the Paris 2024 Olympics at age 17, becoming the youngest-ever male medalist in Olympic table tennis. Also won gold at the 2023 European Games, reached world #4 by November 2024, and became the first French player to win a WTT Champions tournament.

name: Youssoufa Moukoko
milestone: Made his Bundesliga debut for Borussia Dortmund at age 16 (November 21, 2020), becoming the youngest player in Bundesliga history, and became the league's youngest scorer 27 days later. Won the DFB-Pokal (German Cup) with Dortmund in 2021 and the UEFA U21 European Championship with Germany in 2021.

name: Ban Hyo-jin
milestone: Won gold medal in the women's 10m air rifle at the Paris 2024 Olympics at age 16, setting an Olympic record in qualification and becoming South Korea's youngest-ever Olympic gold medalist and the youngest-ever female Olympic champion in shooting.

name: Paolo Banchero
milestone: Selected #1 overall in the 2022 NBA Draft and named NBA Rookie of the Year in 2023 at age 20. Became an NBA All-Star at 21 (the youngest player in the 2024 All-Star Game) and has established himself as a franchise cornerstone for the Orlando Magic.

name: Stephon Castle
milestone: Selected #4 overall in the 2024 NBA Draft and named NBA Rookie of the Year for the 2024-25 season at age 20. Won the NCAA national championship with UConn in 2024 and reached the NBA Finals with the San Antonio Spurs in 2026.

name: Hezly Rivera
milestone: Won Olympic team gold medal at the Paris 2024 Olympics at age 16 as the youngest Team USA athlete at the Games. Also won the 2023 junior U.S. national championship and the 2025 U.S. senior national championship.

name: Finneas O'Connell
milestone: Won five Grammy Awards at the 62nd Grammy Awards on January 26, 2020, at age 22, including Producer of the Year, Non-Classical (the youngest winner in Grammy history), Best Engineered Album, and shared Album/Record/Song of the Year for producing Billie Eilish's debut album.

name: Charli D'Amelio
milestone: Became the first TikTok creator to reach 100 million followers in November 2020 at age 16, and was the most-followed creator on the platform from March 2020 to June 2022, earning an estimated $70 million in two years per Forbes.

name: Addison Rae
milestone: Signed with talent agency WME in January 2020 at age 19, joined The Hype House in December 2019, amassed 88M+ TikTok followers, and was one of the highest-earning TikTok personalities by 2020, later releasing her debut single 'Obsessed' (2021) and starring in Netflix's 'He's All That' (2021).

name: Bella Poarch
milestone: Created the most-liked video on TikTok in August 2020 at age 23 (a lip-sync to Millie B's 'M to the B' with 56M+ likes), signed with Warner Records in 2021, and released debut single 'Build a Bitch' which charted at #56 on the Billboard Hot 100 and was the most-watched music video on YouTube in its first 24 hours.

name: Loren Gray
milestone: Signed a record deal with Virgin Records in March 2018 at age 15, released debut single 'My Story' in August 2018, and was the most-followed person on TikTok from March 2019 to March 2020 with 50M+ followers, earning $2.4 million in 2019 per Forbes.

name: Maggie Rogers
milestone: Her song 'Alaska' went viral in 2016 at age 22 after a video of Pharrell Williams's visibly moved reaction during a master class at NYU gained millions of views, leading to a major label deal; her debut album 'Heard It in a Past Life' debuted at #2 on the Billboard 200 in January 2019, and she was nominated for Grammy Best New Artist in 2020.

name: Lewis Capaldi
milestone: His single 'Someone You Loved' topped the UK Singles Chart for seven weeks in March 2019 at age 22, reached #1 on the US Billboard Hot 100 in November 2019, and his debut album 'Divinely Uninspired to a Hellish Extent' was the best-selling UK album of 2019 and 2020; he won the 2020 Brit Awards for Song of the Year and Best New Artist.

name: Lindsey Jordan (Snail Mail)
milestone: Signed a recording contract with Matador Records in September 2017 at age 18, and released debut studio album 'Lush' in June 2018 to critical acclaim, reaching #2 on the Billboard Heatseekers Albums chart and earning widespread indie press coverage including Pitchfork's Best New Music designation.

name: Nikkie de Jager (NikkieTutorials)
milestone: Her YouTube video 'The Power of Makeup' went viral in 2015 at age 21, inspiring a global movement; Forbes named her one of the top 10 beauty influencers in 2017; she won the Shorty Award for YouTube Guru and Teen Choice Award for Choice Fashion/Beauty Web Star in 2017; and she became Global Beauty Adviser for Marc Jacobs Beauty in January 2019.

name: Josh Richards
milestone: Co-founded TalentX Entertainment, became Chief Strategy Officer of Triller, and signed a recording contract with Warner Records in July 2020 at age 18; earned an estimated $5 million in 2021 per Forbes, making him the fourth highest-earning TikTok personality, with 25.7M TikTok followers.

name: Noah Beck
milestone: Went viral on TikTok in 2020 at age 19, was listed as one of TikTok's Top 10 breakout content creators of 2020, joined the Sway House collective, and amassed 33M+ TikTok followers with 1.5B+ likes by age 20, securing partnerships with FIFA, MLS, and major fashion brands.

name: Rod Wave
milestone: His single 'Heart on Ice' went viral on TikTok and peaked at #25 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 2019 at age 21; debut album 'Ghetto Gospel' peaked at #10 on the Billboard 200 in November 2019; and second album 'Pray 4 Love' peaked at #2 on the Billboard 200 in April 2020, with 'Rags2Riches' reaching #12 on the Hot 100.

name: Shayne Coplan
milestone: Founded Polymarket in June 2020 at age 22, building a blockchain-based prediction market that became one of the world's largest prediction platforms, and became the world's youngest self-made billionaire at age 27 in 2025.

name: Laura Deming
milestone: Founded The Longevity Fund in 2011 at age 17, the first venture capital firm dedicated to funding aging and life-extension biotech companies, after being named a Thiel Fellow and dropping out of MIT at age 14.

name: Simon Tian
milestone: Founded Neptune in January 2013 at age 18, launched the Neptune Pine smartwatch on Kickstarter raising over $800,000 in 30 days, and was named a 2015 Thiel Fellow, with the device shipping by August 2014 and becoming available through Best Buy and Amazon.

name: Blake Resnick
milestone: Founded BRINC Drones in 2019 at age 18 (initial work began at 17 in 2017), received a Thiel Fellowship in 2020, was named the youngest honoree on Forbes 30 Under 30 in 2022, and raised a $25 million Series A in 2021 at age 21, building a drone company valued at $300 million by 2023.

name: Awais Ahmed
milestone: Co-founded Pixxel Space Technologies in February 2019 at age 20-21, building India's first private hyperspectral satellite company, and was named to Fortune India 40 Under 40 in 2022 at age 23-24, with Pixxel launching its first satellites and securing a NASA contract.

name: Luana Lopes Lara
milestone: Co-founded Kalshi in 2018 at age 22 with Tarek Mansour, entered Y Combinator's Winter 2019 batch, and built the first federally regulated prediction market exchange in the United States, later becoming the world's youngest self-made woman billionaire at age 29.

name: Pulkit Jaiswal
milestone: Founded Garuda Robotics at age 19 (around 2012), a regional leader in aerial drone fleet applications in Southeast Asia, and then founded SwarmX in 2015 at age 22, building autonomous drone platforms for government security applications and being named an MIT Technology Review Innovator Under 35.

name: Iyinoluwa Aboyeji
milestone: Co-founded Andela in 2014 at age 23, which received $24M Series B funding from Mark Zuckerberg in 2016, and co-founded Flutterwave in 2016 at age 25, both later becoming unicorns.

name: Rashid Khan
milestone: Made ODI debut for Afghanistan at age 17 in October 2015; became the youngest captain in international cricket history at 19, and the fastest bowler to 100 ODI wickets (44 matches) by age 19 in March 2018.

name: Naseem Shah
milestone: Made Test debut for Pakistan at age 16 in November 2019, becoming the ninth-youngest Test debutant; took a five-wicket haul at age 16 in December 2019 and became the youngest bowler to take a Test hat-trick in February 2020 at age 16.

name: Mujeeb Ur Rahman
milestone: Made ODI debut for Afghanistan at age 16 in December 2017, taking 4/24 on debut; became the youngest player to take a five-wicket haul in ODI cricket at age 16 in February 2018, and played in Afghanistan's first-ever Test match in June 2018.

name: Rema
milestone: Signed with Jonzing World/Mavin Records in 2019 at age 19; debut EP topped Apple Music Nigeria charts, and breakout single 'Dumebi' became a viral hit with 85M+ YouTube views, landing on Barack Obama's summer playlist.

name: Tyla
milestone: Signed with Epic Records in 2021 at age 19 following domestic success of debut single 'Getting Late'; later won the inaugural Grammy Award for Best African Music Performance in 2024 at age 22 for 'Water,' becoming the youngest African artist to win a Grammy.

name: Abbas Sajwani
milestone: Founded AHS Group in 2017 at age 18 and launched AHS Properties in 2021 at age 22, building a multi-billion-dollar luxury real estate development company in Dubai; named to Forbes Middle East 30 Under 30 in 2024 and became the youngest Arab billionaire in 2026.

name: Shubman Gill
milestone: Named Player of the Tournament at the 2018 ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup at age 18, scoring 418 runs at an average of 104.50; made ODI debut for India in January 2019 at age 19, and was bought by Kolkata Knight Riders in the IPL for Rs 1.8 crore.

name: Shaheen Shah Afridi
milestone: Made T20I debut for Pakistan in April 2018 at age 18, becoming the first cricketer born after 2000 to represent Pakistan; completed all-format debuts in 2018, and was named ICC Men's Cricketer of the Year in 2021 at age 21, the first Pakistani to win the Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy.

name: Samuel Takyi
milestone: Won Olympic bronze medal in men's featherweight boxing at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics (held in 2021) at age 20, becoming Ghana's first Olympic boxing medalist since 1972 and Ghana's only medalist at the Tokyo Olympics.

name: Ayman Sadiq
milestone: Founded 10 Minute School in 2015 at age 23, Bangladesh's largest online education platform; won the Queen's Young Leaders Award 2018 and was named to Forbes 30 Under 30 Asia in 2018, reaching over 150,000 students online.

name: Tems
milestone: Released debut EP 'For Broken Ears' in 2020 at age 25 and was featured on Wizkid's 'Essence' which peaked at #9 on the Billboard Hot 100, earning a Grammy nomination; also featured on Drake's 'Certified Lover Boy' album in 2021.

name: Mohammed Rabii
milestone: Won gold at the 2015 AIBA World Amateur Championships in Doha at age 22, becoming the first Moroccan and first Arab boxer to win world championship gold; won bronze at the 2016 Rio Olympics at age 23, and was named WSB Boxer of the Year in 2015.

name: Gukesh Dommaraju
milestone: Won the FIDE World Chess Championship in December 2024 at age 18, defeating Ding Liren to become the youngest undisputed world chess champion in history.

name: Nodirbek Abdusattorov
milestone: Won the FIDE World Rapid Chess Championship in December 2021 at age 17, defeating Magnus Carlsen and Ian Nepomniachtchi to become the youngest ever World Rapid Champion.

name: Syed Sumail Hassan
milestone: Won The International 2015 with Evil Geniuses at age 16, becoming the youngest player to win The International and the youngest esports player to surpass $1 million in career winnings.

name: Topias Taavitsainen
milestone: Won The International 2018 with OG at age 20, coming from open qualifiers to claim the championship and over $11 million in prize money, then repeated as champion in 2019.

name: Lee Sang-hyeok
milestone: Won the League of Legends World Championship in 2013 at age 17 with SK Telecom T1, and went on to win five more World Championships by age 26, becoming the most decorated LoL player in history.

name: Yu Wenbo
milestone: Won the 2018 League of Legends World Championship with Invictus Gaming at age 17, becoming the first Chinese bot laner to win Worlds and the first LPL team to claim the title.

name: Danil Kryshkovets
milestone: Won the Perfect World Shanghai Major 2024 with Team Spirit at age 17, becoming the youngest-ever CS Major champion and MVP while recording the highest individual rating ever at a Major.

name: Valerii Vakhovskyi
milestone: Won the PGL Major Stockholm 2021 with Natus Vincere at age 18, also becoming the youngest Intel Grand Slam winner at 18 years and 250 days old.

name: Gennady Korotkevich
milestone: Won the ICPC World Finals in 2013 at age 18 with ITMO University, having already won six consecutive IOI gold medals from 2007-2012, establishing himself as the greatest competitive programmer of all time.

name: Benjamin Qi
milestone: Won back-to-back IOI gold medals in 2018 and 2019, finishing 1st place both times, becoming one of only four programmers in the world to win IOI multiple times.

name: Anathan Pham
milestone: Won The International 2018 with OG at age 18, then repeated as champion in 2019, becoming part of the first team to win back-to-back TI titles and developing a novel carry Io strategy that revolutionized the meta.

name: Saul Leonardo Mena II
milestone: Won the Capcom Cup 2017 at age 18, defeating reigning EVO champion Tokido in the grand finals to claim the $250,000 first prize, the largest ever awarded at a fighting game tournament at the time.

name: Allan Alvarez
milestone: Set the world record in Super Mario 64 120-star category in May 2017 at age 22, becoming the first person to complete the category in under 100 minutes, and held the record on multiple occasions.

name: Alex Tan
milestone: Set the world record for speedrunning Super Mario World in 2015 at age 19, completing the game in 1 minute and 38 seconds using arbitrary code execution, and created the Guinness World Record-holding most difficult level in Super Mario Maker.

name: Shashvat Nakrani
milestone: Co-founded BharatPe in 2018 at age 19 while a student at IIT Delhi, building it into a fintech company valued at $2.9 billion by 2021 and becoming the youngest person on the IIFL Wealth Hurun India Rich List at age 23.

name: Liu Jingkang (JK Liu)
milestone: Founded Insta360 (Arashi Vision) in 2014 at age 23 while a senior at Nanjing University, creating a panoramic camera company that later became a global market leader.

name: Kennedy Ekezie
milestone: Co-founded Kippa, a fintech bookkeeping platform for African SMEs, in 2021 at age 23, which raised over $11.6M and onboarded 800,000+ businesses; also received Queen's Young Leader Award from Queen Elizabeth II in 2018 at age 20.

name: Shane Curran
milestone: Won the BT Young Scientist and Technology Exhibition in January 2017 at age 16 for qCrypt quantum-secure encryption, was named to Forbes 30 Under 30 in 2018 at 17, and founded Evervault in 2018-2019 at age 18-19, raising $3.2M seed from Sequoia Capital by October 2019.

name: Hany Rashwan
milestone: Founded Payout.com, an enterprise fintech company, in late 2014 at age 24, which processed over $50M in loans by its second year and raised $4.75M led by Tim Draper; named to Forbes 30 Under 30 in 2017.

name: Ferry Unardi
milestone: Co-founded Traveloka, Southeast Asia's largest online travel agency, in March 2012 at age 24 after leaving Harvard Business School, launching the platform publicly in October 2012.

name: The Kid Laroi
milestone: At age 18, his single 'Stay' with Justin Bieber topped the Billboard Hot 100 (August 2021), and his debut mixtape 'F*ck Love' reached #1 on the Billboard 200 (July 2021).

name: Megan Moroney
milestone: At age 25, her debut album 'Lucky' reached the top 40 of the Billboard 200 (May 2023) and her single 'Tennessee Orange' charted on the Billboard Hot 100 (2022), making her one of country music's breakout stars before turning 26.

name: Ella Langley
milestone: At age 25, her debut single 'You Look Like You Love Me' with Riley Green reached #1 on the Billboard Country Airplay chart and won Musical Event of the Year at the CMA Awards (November 2024).

name: Cris MJ
milestone: At age 20, 'Una Noche en Medellín' peaked at #22 on Billboard's Hot Latin Songs (2022); at 22, 'Gata Only' with FloyyMenor reached #4 on the Billboard Global 200 and topped the US Hot Latin Songs chart (February 2024), becoming one of the year's biggest Latin hits.

name: FloyyMenor
milestone: At age 18, his hit single 'Gata Only' with Cris MJ reached #4 on the Billboard Global 200 and topped the US Hot Latin Songs chart (February 2024), becoming one of the year's biggest global Latin hits.
